@@ -0,0 +1,42 @@
+import { memo } from 'react';
+import { sizeClass } from './sizeClass';
+import type { SkeletonSize } from './skeletonSize';
+
+type SkeletonProps = {
+  shape: 'text' | 'circle' | 'block';
+  width: SkeletonSize;
+  height: SkeletonSize;
+};
+
+const SHAPE_CLASS: Record<'text' | 'circle' | 'block', string> = {
+  text: 'rounded',
+  circle: 'rounded-full',
+  block: 'rounded-card',
+};
+
+// sizeClass entries are complete box classes (both a w- and an h- class),
+// so concatenating two entries for independent width/height props would
+// emit two classes per dimension whose winner depends on Tailwind's
+// generated CSS order rather than on the props. Each dimension keeps
+// only its own half of the pair.
+function dimensionClass(size: SkeletonSize, prefix: 'w-' | 'h-'): string {
+  const classNames = sizeClass[size].split(' ');
+  const match = classNames.find((name) => name.startsWith(prefix));
+  if (match === undefined) {
+    throw new Error(`sizeClass.${size} has no ${prefix} class`);
+  }
+  return match;
+}
+
+export const Skeleton = memo(function Skeleton({
+  shape,
+  width,
+  height,
+}: SkeletonProps) {
+  return (
+    <span
+      aria-hidden="true"
+      className={`inline-block animate-pulse bg-surface-hover ${SHAPE_CLASS[shape]} ${dimensionClass(width, 'w-')} ${dimensionClass(height, 'h-')}`}
+    />
+  );
+});

+  it('takes the first letter of the first and last word', () => {

+  });
+
+  it('uses a single letter for a one-word name', () => {
+    expect(deriveInitials('Cher')).toBe('C');
+  });
+
+  it('collapses extra whitespace between words', () => {
+    expect(deriveInitials('  Grace   Hopper  ')).toBe('GH');
+  });
+
+  it('returns an empty string for an empty name', () => {
+    expect(deriveInitials('')).toBe('');
+  });
+
+  it('uppercases lowercase input', () => {
+    expect(deriveInitials('ada lovelace')).toBe('AL');
+  });
+});
diff --git a/src/shared/ui/deriveInitials.ts b/src/shared/ui/deriveInitials.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..378aadd

+++ b/src/shared/ui/deriveInitials.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,8 @@
+export function deriveInitials(displayName: string): string {
+  const words = displayName.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
+  if (words.length === 0) return '';
+
+  const first = words[0]?.[0] ?? '';
+  const last = words.length > 1 ? (words[words.length - 1]?.[0] ?? '') : '';
+  return (first + last).toUpperCase();
+}

specs/ARCHITECTURE.md:155:## 6. Decision log
specs/ARCHITECTURE.md:159:- **React Router library mode over framework mode** - keeps Vite the only build tool and the output static, which matches the hosting constraint. Framework mode brings routing machinery, typegen and a server story this app never uses.
specs/ARCHITECTURE.md:170:- **No `frame-ancestors` in the CSP meta tag; the response header instead** (2026-08-13, phase 1) - browsers ignore `frame-ancestors` when it arrives in a meta tag and log a warning saying so, so including it would buy no protection while producing a permanent console warning, forcing an allow-list entry into the e2e console assertion that otherwise stays empty. Rejected: keeping the directive in the meta tag as a statement of intent. Framing protection therefore ships as a response header, which Cloudflare Pages sets from a `_headers` file in the build output - the one thing the previous hosting choice could not do. Everything else stays in the meta tag, so there is one policy to read rather than two half-policies.
specs/ARCHITECTURE.md:171:- **Cloudflare Pages over GitHub Pages** (2026-08-13, phase 1) - the repository is private, and GitHub Pages does not serve a site from a private repository on this account's plan, so the hosting decision had to be remade rather than debated. Cloudflare Pages serves the site at the root (no project sub-path, so the Vite `base` stays `/`), gives SPA deep links through a `_redirects` rule instead of a `404.html` copy, and sets response headers from `_headers`, which is what makes framing protection possible at all. Deployment stays inside the same GitHub Actions workflow, running `wrangler pages deploy` after every gate has passed, so the rule that a deploy follows a green pipeline is unchanged. Rejected: Cloudflare's own Git integration, which builds and deploys on push without waiting for the workflow's gates, giving up exactly that property; and making the repository public to keep Pages, which is not a hosting decision.
specs/ARCHITECTURE.md:172:- **App entry budget of 100 kB gzipped** (2026-08-13, phase 1) - set against an estimate of 85-90 kB for the fixed dependency set (react-dom, react-router, zod, i18next, react-i18next, web-vitals), leaving roughly 10-15% headroom. Rejected: 75 kB, which the dependency set alone would likely bust, turning the budget into noise the first time it ran; and deferring the number until measured, which leaves CI with no size gate while the skeleton is built. Per-route chunks stay at 30 kB.
specs/ARCHITECTURE.md:173:- **App entry budget revised to 150 kB gzipped** (2026-08-13, phase 1) - wiring the real router in M5 step 31 measured the entry at 112.77 kB, busting the 100 kB budget by 12.77 kB. An isolated esbuild probe (`createBrowserRouter` + `RouterProvider` alone, tree-shaken, react/react-dom externalized) put react-router's own weight at ~31 kB gzipped - the original 85-90 kB estimate undercounted react-router specifically, this was not a tree-shaking regression or a code defect. Per this section's own rule, a wrong estimate is revisited with the user rather than silently raised; the user set the corrected number at 150 kB, leaving headroom over the measured 112.77 kB rather than pinning the limit to the exact current build. Rejected: a code-splitting mitigation to defer router construction, which was not pursued because the router must exist to render the very first route - there is no idle window before it that deferral could exploit.
specs/ARCHITECTURE.md:174:- **Two design tokens darkened past their mockup literals: `border-field` and `ink-faint`** (2026-08-13, phase 1) - `docs/reference.md`'s pulled values (`#E2DDEE` field border, `#8E8AA0` faint ink) hold 1.33:1 and 3.34:1/4.31:1 (light/dark) against the surfaces they sit on, both short of invariant 72's AA floor (3:1 for UI boundaries, 4.5:1 for body text - the correlation id `ErrorState` renders in `ink-faint`, per invariant 92, is body text). `theme.css` re-declares both tokens (`border-field` `#8F89A3`, `ink-faint` `#726E85` light / `#847F95` dark) with `contrastPairs.test.ts` entries proving the new values clear AA in both themes. Rejected: keeping the mockup literals and accepting the AA failure, which invariant 70's mockup-fidelity goal does not outrank invariant 72's binding accessibility floor; and reusing an existing darker token (`ink-muted`) for the correlation id instead of darkening `ink-faint`, which would collapse two intentionally distinct text weights into one.
specs/ARCHITECTURE.md:176:## 7. Deliberately not built
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:1:# Product spec: phase-1-setup - a deployable, instrumented skeleton with no features in it
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:3:## Summary
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:7:## User stories
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:17:## Behavior (numbered invariants)
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:19:Every invariant is observable: a test, a lint rule, a CI job or a reviewer with the deployed URL can decide it. "Fails lint" means `npm run lint` exits non-zero with an error (not a warning) that names the rule.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:21:### Layer boundaries and their enforcement
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:30:8. `shared` and `platform` are domain-free: no exported name, type, prop, constant or catalogue key in either layer references a domain concept (user, manager, hierarchy, tree, session, login, credential, and the reporting-line sense of "report" - `directReports`, `reportCount`). The mechanical check matches whole identifier segments, not substrings, against a stated allow-list, because a substring match would fail against `encodeURIComponent`, `URLSearchParams` and a `missing-key-reporter` module. A domain type appearing in a `shared` or `platform` signature is a review failure and a defect against this invariant; that half is review-carried in this phase, because no domain type exists yet to detect.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:31:9. Two feature slices exist - `features/auth` and `features/hierarchy` - each with a public entry and no product behavior behind it. They exist so that phases 2 and 3 add code inside an established slice, and so that invariant 6 is demonstrable.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:36:### Configuration
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:45:20. Nothing in configuration is secret. The bundle is public, so any value that would be a secret is by definition not a configuration value in this app - see invariant 133.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:47:### HTTP client
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:53:25. A caller-initiated abort is not a failure. It is never retried, is never reported as an application error, and is returned as its own `cancelled` outcome, distinct from every failure the client can produce (invariant 33). A caller that cancels a request on unmount cannot render an error state by mistake, because there is no failure value to render. A signal that is already aborted when the client is called yields `cancelled` with no transport call at all.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:58:30. Every outbound request carries a W3C `traceparent` header in valid format, with a fresh span id per request and a trace id equal to the correlation id for the interaction (invariant 47).
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:61:33. A call has exactly three outcomes: success, failure and cancelled. **Failures** are exactly one of four types: `NetworkError`, `TimeoutError`, `HttpError` (carrying the status code) and `ParseError`. That four-member union is exhaustive and discriminable by a literal tag, so a `switch` over it typechecks without a default branch. The union describes failures only - cancellation (invariant 25) is a sibling outcome, not a fifth member, so adding cancellation does not widen it.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:65:### Caching - withdrawn (36-44)
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:67:Caching is out of scope, for this phase and for the roadmap. The withdrawn design, its nine invariants and the ten review findings it absorbed are preserved in [../CACHE.md](../CACHE.md). Specifying it produced the largest single piece of this document - a six-state entry machine, per-key generations, revalidation cooldowns and their tests - to save one 9KB request against a dataset of 33 users. ARCHITECTURE.md's decision log records the withdrawal; nothing in phases 1 to 3 builds `platform/cache`, and the repository per resource is the seam a cache attaches behind if it is ever worth its complexity.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:69:36. through 44. **Withdrawn.** The numbers are retired rather than reused, so every invariant from 45 onward keeps the identity it carries in the review record, in `loop.json` and in TECH.md's testing map. A future loop that reintroduces caching writes new invariants under its own numbering.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:71:One rule from the withdrawn set survives on its own merit, and it moves to invariant 128 rather than staying here: nothing in this phase writes to `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB or a service worker cache, and the lint rule banning those globals is installed in phase 1.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:73:### Observability
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:75:45. The observability **facade** exposes exactly three interfaces: logger, tracer, analytics - no fourth key. No module outside `platform/observability` imports or constructs a sink. This invariant is about the facade's surface, not about the factory's return value; see invariant 45a.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:76:45a. The factory that builds observability returns two values: the facade of invariant 45, and a read handle on the ring buffer when the buffer sink is selected (otherwise nothing). The handle exists so e2e can read what was recorded (invariant 49) without any module importing a sink. Attaching that handle to a global belongs to exactly one module in `app`, is gated on a configuration flag, and is a lint failure anywhere else. `platform` never writes to `globalThis`.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:84:52. Web Vitals LCP, INP and CLS are collected through the `web-vitals` package and reported through the same facade, as the metrics they are actually named after. `PerformanceObserver` alone cannot compute INP's percentile-with-windowing rule or CLS's session-window maximum, and reporting a maximum interaction latency under the label `INP` would make the telemetry lie. The dependency is a deliberate exception to invariant 134, recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md's decision log.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:93:### Internationalization
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:105:### The shared UI kit
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:110:72. Both themes hold WCAG AA: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text, icons and UI boundaries. This is asserted by an automated contrast check over the token pairs the components actually use, not eyeballed against the mockup.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:114:76. `Skeleton` reserves the dimensions of the content it stands in for, so swapping skeleton for content produces no layout shift. Dimensions arrive as a closed set of kit-local size tokens shared with the content, and the component emits **no `style` attribute** - the production CSP sets `style-src 'self'` with no `'unsafe-inline'`, so an inline width or height would be blocked by the browser and would raise the CSP violation invariant 100 forbids. The proof is a browser measurement: the skeleton's box and its replacement content's box are equal.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:125:86a. A development-only kit route exists at `/__kit`, mounted only when a build-time flag is on, rendering every documented state of all eight components from one shared state inventory. Playwright exercises that route at a 320px viewport with axe, in real light and real dark (the browser's `colorScheme`, not a stubbed media query), and measures the skeleton-to-content swap of invariant 76. This is a narrow verification surface, not a design-system site: it has no navigation, no documentation prose and no link from the app.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:127:87. Every kit component is covered by unit tests that render each of its documented states and assert zero axe violations. Those unit assertions run in light only: jsdom applies no stylesheet, so a dark run there would assert the same DOM twice and prove nothing. Dark-theme axe coverage is the browser run on the kit route (invariant 86a). "Documented states" is a single inventory module consumed by both the unit tests and the kit route, and a check fails when a component exported from the kit has no state in it.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:129:### The app shell
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:140:96a. The `/login` placeholder is generic. It uses kit components, catalogue strings, the login canvas token and the type scale, but carries none of mockup screen `1a`'s chrome: no nav rail, no centered login card, no brand mark. Screen `1a` is built once, in phase 2, where it can be compared against the mockup in a single pass. Building the card shell here would be feature-shaped code with no behavior behind it, which invariant 136 forbids.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:143:99. The delivered HTML carries a Content-Security-Policy meta tag that at minimum sets `default-src 'self'`, `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'self'`, and a `connect-src` that includes the configured API base URL. It does NOT set `frame-ancestors`: that directive is ignored inside a meta tag and browsers warn about it, so including it would buy nothing and force a console allow-list entry that invariant 100 depends on staying empty. Clickjacking protection is a response header instead - see invariant 99a. `img-src` allows only `'self'` and `data:` - no remote host. Phase 3 reads the live `users` payload, learns the actual avatar hosts, and widens `img-src` as a reviewed change with a decision-log entry. Shipping a permissive `img-src` now, before there is evidence of which hosts are needed, is explicitly rejected.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:144:99a. Framing protection ships as a response header, because the meta tag cannot carry it. The build output contains a `_headers` file declaring `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'` for every path, which Cloudflare Pages serves as a real header. It is deliberately the only directive in the header: the meta tag stays the single place the rest of the policy is read, and two half-policies that can disagree is the failure mode this split avoids. That exclusivity is **asserted, not just described**: the build-output check compares `dist/_headers` against its exact expected content byte for byte - the `/*` path line and the one indented header line and nothing else - so an added directive fails the check exactly as a missing one does. An exact-content assertion is what the sibling `_redirects` check already uses (invariant 124), and it is required here for a second reason: Cloudflare's `_headers` format silently ignores a header line that is not indented under its path block, so a containment check would pass a file that ships no framing protection at all. The deployed smoke run then asserts the header actually arrives on the live response, which is the only check that can distinguish a correct file from a correctly-formatted file the host did not apply. The residual gap the previous hosting choice left - no framing protection at all - is closed rather than recorded.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:145:100. No route produces a CSP violation, and the console carries no error or warning, in both the development server and the production build. React's root is created with `onCaughtError` and `onUncaughtError` handlers that route boundary-caught errors to the observability facade instead of the default `console.error`, so an error the app handles never reaches the console. The allow-list is empty for every spec but one. The forced-error spec aborts a lazy route chunk, and an aborted subresource makes the BROWSER log a network error that no application code can intercept; that spec therefore asserts an exact expected set - the single aborted-request entry, matched by URL - and fails on any other entry. An exact expected set is not an open-ended allow-list: it fails on a new entry exactly as an empty assertion would, which is the property this invariant depends on. Widening it, or adding an entry to any other spec, requires the same argument as downgrading a lint rule.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:148:### The quality pipeline
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:150:102. Each **gating check** is one npm script, and CI runs exactly those scripts. There is no gate that exists only in the workflow file, so a check that passes locally passes in CI for the same reason. Infrastructure setup steps are exempt and named explicitly - `npm ci` and `npx playwright install` are the whole allow-list; a run line that is neither an npm script nor an allow-listed setup command fails the workflow-parse test. The rule's scope is the **`verify` job**, which is where every gate lives. The `deploy` job is not a gate - it runs only after `verify` has passed, only on `main`, and it cannot make a failing change green - so its steps are outside this rule. That is not a loophole for smuggling a check into the workflow: the deploy job's one assertion (invariant 123's deployment-URL comparison) is about the deployment itself, which by definition has no local equivalent to run, and it is the only such step this phase permits. A new `run:` line in the `deploy` job that checks the *code* rather than the deployment is a violation of this invariant's intent and is caught in review.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:160:112. Size budgets are checked by `size-limit` against the production build, and every emitted chunk class has an entry: the initial payload (entry plus vendor) at most 150 kB gzipped, the stylesheet at most 15 kB gzipped, each per-route chunk at most 30 kB gzipped, and each lazily loaded catalogue chunk at most 5 kB gzipped. Exceeding a budget fails CI with actual and limit printed. The figure was originally set at 100 kB against an estimate of 85-90 kB for the **fixed runtime dependency set alone** (react-dom, react-router, zod, i18next, react-i18next, web-vitals). Wiring the real router in M5 measured the entry at 112.77 kB and busted that number; an isolated tree-shaken probe of `createBrowserRouter`/`RouterProvider` alone put react-router's own weight at roughly 31 kB gzipped, showing the original estimate had undercounted react-router specifically rather than the build regressing. Per this invariant's own rule, the number was revisited with the user rather than silently raised, and the user set the corrected budget at 150 kB. That is measured from the first milestone rather than the last, and if a future measurement contradicts the estimate again the number is again revisited with the user, never silently raised.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:163:115. Unit and e2e runs are deterministic. Time and randomness are injected, no test depends on wall-clock timing or on a real host, and a test attempting real network access fails.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:171:### Deployment
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:175:122. The site is served from the root of its own hostname, so the Vite base path is `/` and every asset and route URL is root-relative. No URL in the built output carries a project sub-path, and a stale `/hierarchy-tree/` prefix anywhere in `dist` fails the build-output check.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:176:123. The deployed site renders the placeholder home route at its root URL. The URL is the Cloudflare Pages project's production hostname, recorded **once, in one machine-readable place** - `deployment.json` at the repository root, holding the project name and the production hostname - so that the workflow, the deployed Playwright project and the documentation all read the same value rather than each carrying a copy that can drift. A prose document cannot be that place: a workflow step cannot read a sentence out of `VERIFICATION.md`, so recording it only there guarantees a second hardcoded copy in `ci.yml`. `VERIFICATION.md` and `.env.example` cite the value, and a unit test asserts the value they cite matches `deployment.json`, which is what keeps the documentation honest without making it the source. The deploy step additionally asserts that the deployment URL Wrangler reports back **is** that recorded production hostname, not a `<hash>.<project>.pages.dev` preview URL. Without that assertion a mis-configured project (invariant 126) produces a green deploy job that shipped to a preview nobody looks at, which is the one deployment failure the pipeline cannot otherwise see.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:179:126. The deployment depends on manual, one-time setup performed by the repository owner, and the list is exhaustive because every item on it is invisible to CI: a Cloudflare Pages project created with direct-upload (not Git integration, which would deploy without waiting for the gates); **the project's production branch set to `main`**; and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` stored as repository secrets. The token carries the Pages edit permission and nothing else. The production-branch item is load-bearing rather than administrative: Cloudflare decides production-versus-preview by comparing the upload's `--branch` against the project's configured production branch, so if they disagree, `wrangler pages deploy --branch=main` succeeds, reports a preview URL, and leaves the production hostname stale while the job stays green. Invariant 123's URL assertion is what turns that silent case into a failure. This whole list is named as a prerequisite in the change, so a failed first deploy is diagnosable in seconds, and no secret value appears in the repository (invariant 133).
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:181:126a. Invariants 123 and 124 cannot be proven before merge, and the phase does not pretend otherwise. Invariant 121 forbids preview deployments, so no pull-request run produces a URL to test; this is a deliberate trade - preview deploys would make the exit criterion provable on the pull request, and they are rejected because they put a deploy surface and a live token on every pull request, including forks. The consequence is an explicit obligation rather than a gap: after the merge to `main`, the deploy job runs and `npm run e2e:deployed` is run against the recorded production hostname, its output is captured as evidence, and **the phase is not complete until it passes** (invariant 119). If it fails, the phase is not silently done - the failure is the loop's, a fix lands on a follow-up branch through the same gates, and the deployed run is repeated. No milestone boundary and no pull-request run may claim invariants 123 or 124 as verified.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:183:### What must not be true at the end of this phase
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:186:128. No session exists: there is no logged-in user concept, no route guard and no logout. Nothing in the app writes to `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB or a service worker cache, and a use of any of those globals in `src` fails lint - the rule that carries the storage half of this invariant, inherited from the withdrawn caching set. The banned set is enumerated, not illustrative: `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `indexedDB`, `caches` (the `CacheStorage` global, which is the service-worker cache this invariant names) and `navigator.serviceWorker`. Each is banned in **both** the bare-identifier and the member forms - `window.localStorage`, `globalThis.sessionStorage` and their siblings - because a bare-identifier rule alone matches neither, which is the same pairing the network ban of invariant 21 already uses. A storage global reached by computed member access is not lint-detectable; that residue is review-carried and named as such. Phase 2 removes the `sessionStorage` entry from that rule with a decision-log line, because the session record is what first needs it.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:192:134. No runtime dependency is added beyond what these invariants require, and each added dependency is justified against the size budget. The allow-list is exactly `react`, `react-dom`, `react-router`, `zod`, `i18next`, `react-i18next` and `web-vitals`; a check fails when `dependencies` stops matching it, so a new one is a deliberate edit rather than a drift. Specifically excluded: no data-fetching library, no component library, no telemetry vendor SDK, no polyfill for something the pinned Node and target browsers already have. `web-vitals` is on the list by the explicit decision recorded at invariant 52, not by default.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:196:## Goals / Non-goals
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:219:- Response caching - in-flight dedupe, TTL, stale-while-revalidate. Withdrawn from the roadmap on 2026-08-13, not deferred to a later phase: no phase builds `platform/cache`, and the repository per resource is the seam a cache attaches behind if one is ever wanted. Invariants 36-44 are retired with it.
specs/phase-1-setup/PRODUCT.md:229:- A theme switcher, a design-system documentation site, or a component gallery that ships. The development-only kit route of invariant 86a is in scope and is not a gallery: it is a verification surface that renders the state inventory, carries no documentation and no navigation, and is absent from the production build by invariant 86b. A gallery page reachable by a user of the deployed site remains out of scope.

The live smoke runs under Node, where CORS is not enforced, so the probe cannot discover it. It is recorded as a phase 2 risk in TECH.md rather than as a phase 1 invariant.

specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:21:### Environment and targets
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:24:- Remote is `git@github.com:sergeykhomyuk/hierarchy-tree.git` and the repository is **private**, which is what rules GitHub Pages out and settles the hosting question (ARCHITECTURE.md decision log, 2026-08-13).
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:25:- The site is deployed to a Cloudflare Pages project by direct upload from the CI workflow, after every gate has passed. It serves from the root of `https://<project>.pages.dev`, so the Vite `base` stays `/` and every URL in the build output is root-relative (invariant 122). The repository owner performs the one-time setup: create the Pages project, mint an API token scoped to Cloudflare Pages edit, and store `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` as repository secrets (invariant 126). The production hostname the project is given is recorded in `deployment.json` at the repository root - `{ "projectName": "hierarchy-tree", "productionHostname": "https://<project>.pages.dev" }` - which is the single machine-readable source invariant 123 requires. The deploy job reads it with `jq`, the `deployed` Playwright project takes it as `DEPLOYED_BASE_URL`, and `VERIFICATION.md` and `.env.example` cite it on a line carrying the literal marker `<!-- production-hostname -->` / `# production-hostname:` respectively, and a unit test asserts each marker is PRESENT and that the value on it equals `deployment.json`'s. Requiring presence is the half that matters: a test phrased only as "the cited hostname matches" passes vacuously against a document that cites nothing, which would reinstate the documentation drift `deployment.json` was introduced to close. M6 makes both edits, in the same change that creates `deployment.json` - M1 ships `VERIFICATION.md` without the marker because the Pages project does not exist yet, and M6 adds it. Recording it only in prose would have forced a second, uncheckable copy into `ci.yml`.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:26:- Cloudflare Pages serves `_redirects` and `_headers` files found at the root of the uploaded directory. Vite copies `public/` into `dist/` verbatim, so both files live in `public/` and need no plugin. This is what replaces the `404.html` copy the previous hosting needed, and what makes the `frame-ancestors` response header of invariant 99a possible at all.

specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:43:### Decisions taken during specification
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:45:- **Entry budget set at 100 kB gzipped, not measured first.** The M1 measurement spike is dropped as a spike, but the measurement itself moves to M1: `.size-limit.json` ships in the first milestone with real globs, so `npm run verify` is the full chain from M1 onward and the first number arrives before five milestones of code are written on top of it. 100 kB is set against ARCHITECTURE.md's 85-90 kB estimate for the fixed dependency set alone; the initial-payload entry measures that set plus this repository's own code, so the 10-15 kB difference is the app's budget rather than headroom. The per-route budget is unchanged at 30 kB gzipped, the stylesheet gets its own 15 kB entry and each lazily loaded catalogue chunk its own 5 kB entry. Encoded in PRODUCT.md invariant 112.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:46:- **`webServer` commands pin `--host 127.0.0.1`, confirmed at M5.** Running the M5 e2e suite for the first time, `vite preview`/`vite dev` without an explicit `--host` bound to `localhost`, which this machine resolved to the IPv6 loopback (`::1`) - a real address the server was listening on, but not the IPv4 `127.0.0.1` every `webServer.url`, `baseURL` and route-mock origin in this config targets, so Playwright's readiness probe timed out against a server that was actually up. `--host 127.0.0.1` on both the `preview` and `dev` commands pins the bind address to the one this config already assumed, which is more portable than relying on `localhost` resolving to IPv4 first in every environment (a known source of exactly this kind of environment-dependent flake). Corrects section 6.2's `webServer` command strings to the same effect.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:47:- **Entry budget revised to 150 kB gzipped at M5.** Wiring the real router (step 31) measured the entry at 112.77 kB, busting the 100 kB figure by 12.77 kB. An isolated tree-shaken probe of `createBrowserRouter`/`RouterProvider` alone put react-router's own weight at roughly 31 kB gzipped, so the M1 estimate had undercounted react-router specifically - not a build regression or a tree-shaking failure. Per the same invariant's rule, the number was revisited with the user rather than silently raised; the user set the corrected figure at 150 kB. Every literal `100 kB` figure elsewhere in this document describes the M1-era config as it stood at that milestone and is left as written history; the live number is 150 kB, per PRODUCT.md invariant 112 and `.size-limit.json`.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:48:- **A development-only kit route.** Five of the eight kit components appear on no product surface in this phase, so invariant 86 was unprovable and invariant 87's "both themes" was proving nothing in jsdom. A `/__kit` route, mounted only behind a build-time flag and dropped from the production bundle, renders every documented state from one shared inventory; Playwright exercises it at 320px with axe in real light and real dark. A shipped gallery page remains a non-goal. Encoded in PRODUCT.md invariants 86, 86a, 86b and 87 and in the amended non-goals list.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:49:- **Cancellation is an outcome, not a failure.** The client's result type has three arms - success, failure and cancelled - so invariant 33's four-member failure union stays exactly as it was and stays exhaustive. Encoded in PRODUCT.md invariants 25 and 33.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:50:- **The request deadline is per logical request.** It covers the first attempt, the backoff wait and the retry together, so a caller passing 8000 ms waits at most 8000 ms rather than 16 s plus backoff. Encoded in PRODUCT.md invariant 23.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:51:- **Caching is withdrawn from the phase and from the roadmap.** The cache was the largest single design in this spec - a six-state entry machine, per-key generations, a revalidation cooldown and nine invariants with their tests - and what it buys is avoiding a repeat of one 9KB request over 33 users. The earlier decision that TTL binds to the key rather than to the call is moot with it. Invariants 36-44 are retired, their numbers are not reused, and ARCHITECTURE.md's decision log carries the withdrawal so a later phase does not quietly reintroduce it. The repository per resource stays the seam a cache attaches behind.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:52:- **Deployment moves to Cloudflare Pages.** The repository is private, so GitHub Pages is not available to it. Cloudflare Pages serves from the root of its own hostname, which removes the `/hierarchy-tree/` base path and everything that hung off it, replaces the `404.html` copy with a `_redirects` rule, and adds response headers through `_headers`. The deploy stays inside the GitHub Actions workflow, after the gates, by direct upload of the `dist` that was just verified. Encoded in PRODUCT.md invariants 120-126.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:53:- **`frame-ancestors` moves from the meta tag to a response header.** The directive is ignored inside a meta tag and browsers warn about it, so it is dropped from the meta policy - which keeps the e2e console allow-list empty rather than spending its first entry on a warning about a no-op. It is then set for real in `_headers`, which the new hosting can serve and the old one could not. Encoded in PRODUCT.md invariants 99 and 99a.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:54:- **`web-vitals` is added to the runtime dependency allow-list.** `PerformanceObserver` alone cannot compute INP's percentile-with-windowing rule or CLS's session-window maximum, and reporting an approximation under the label `INP` would make the telemetry lie. The package's standard ESM build is 8,963 bytes raw and about 3.3 kB gzipped whole, which the entry budget absorbs. Encoded in PRODUCT.md invariants 52 and 134.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:56:## Proposed changes
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:58:### 1. Directory layout
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:62:**Their status, stated up front because it changes what a reviewer does with them: these conventions are implementation GUIDANCE, not acceptance criteria.** No invariant encodes them, no lint rule enforces them, and the testing map has no row for them - a kebab-case module, a default-exported route or an unmemoized component would pass the whole specified pipeline. That is deliberate rather than an oversight: PRODUCT.md's preamble promises that every rule *it* states has a check behind it, and adding a filename linter would mean a new dev dependency and a new invariant to carry style. Style is carried by review here. The one place a name is load-bearing rather than stylistic is the route modules, because `size-limit` globs and the chunk assertions are written against the emitted chunk names (section 5.3) - and that is pinned as a build-output assertion, which does not depend on anyone honouring a convention. Where the guidance below and a binding invariant disagree, the invariant wins; the exceptions list says where that already happens.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:66:- A multi-file folder that is a *public surface* has an `index.ts` re-exporting it and containing nothing else - no side effects, no top-level code. This is not universal, and the two exclusions matter. A folder whose modules are deliberately unreachable from outside gets NO barrel: `platform/observability/sinks/` must not have one, because a `sinks/index.ts` is importable as `@platform/observability/sinks`, which the restricted-import pattern of section 2.3 - requiring a segment after `sinks` - does not match, so the barrel would open a lint-legal path to construct a sink outside the facade and quietly defeat invariant 45. A folder of route modules (`app/routing/routes/`) gets none either, because each is reached only through its own dynamic `import()` and a barrel would defeat the per-route code splitting of invariant 89 by pulling every route into one chunk. `shared/theme/` holds CSS and a token module rather than a public API surface, and gets none. Barrels therefore exist in this phase for the feature entries, `app/composition/`, and the kit - and the layout below is the authority on which folders have one.
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:75:- `platform/configuration/environment.ts` exports both `readEnvironment` and `isDevelopmentBuild`. Invariant 13 requires exactly one module to read `import.meta.env`, and it is backed by a lint rule with a single file override; splitting the module into two files would mean two overrides and would make the invariant's own check weaker. The binding invariant wins over the file convention, and the module is one concept - the environment as this app reads it.

specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:119:    bundle-secrets.test.ts        runs assert-no-secrets.mjs --bundle-only (invariants 20, 133)
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:123:    spa-fallback.test.ts          `_redirects` and `_headers` in `dist` (invariants 99a, 124)
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:131:    favicon.svg                   replaced with an app favicon (invariant 101)
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:132:    _redirects                    `/* /index.html 200` - SPA deep links (invariant 124)
specs/phase-1-setup/TECH.md:133:    _headers                      `frame-ancestors 'none'` (invariant 99a)
