  1050	- 99a - script + deployed: `build-output/spa-fallback.test.ts` asserts `dist/_headers` matches its expected content EXACTLY - the `/*` path line, one indented `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'` line, and nothing else - rather than merely containing that directive. The exactness is doing two jobs. It enforces 99a's "only directive" clause, which a containment check leaves entirely unasserted, so a later edit adding `script-src` or `connect-src` to `_headers` would create the two-disagreeing-policies failure mode the split exists to prevent and would pass. And it catches the format error that actually ships broken protection: Cloudflare's `_headers` syntax requires the header line to be indented under its path block and silently ignores a line that is not, so a mis-indented file passes any containment check while delivering no framing protection at all. Even exact content is still only a file check - `vite preview` sets no headers, so no local run can prove the header is served. The discriminating half is `deployed-smoke.spec.ts`, which reads the response headers of the live document and asserts the directive arrives. Both halves are named because neither alone distinguishes a correct file from a correct file the host did not apply.
  1051	- 101 - unit: `index.html` is parsed and asserted to carry `lang`, the viewport meta, a title, and a favicon link resolving to a file that is not the Vite logo.
  1052
  1053	### Quality pipeline (102-119)
  1054
  1055	- 102 - unit: the workflow-parse test (section 7.1), whose command rule applies to gating steps and exempts the named infrastructure allow-list (`npm ci`, `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`). Without that exemption the test fails against the workflow this spec itself specifies.
  1056	- 103 - unit: the same test asserts step order, now seven steps including `verify:build` after `build`.
  1057	- 104 - CI: `npm run typecheck` is a step; a unit test asserts `tsconfig.app.json` has `"strict": true` so a later removal fails the suite rather than silently weakening the build.
  1058	- 105 - lint, demonstrated failing on an added `any` and an added `!` in the M2 evidence run; plus the suppression grep in `assert-no-secrets.mjs`.
  1059	- 106 - CI: lint is its own step; the six evidence captures show the rule id in each message.
  1060	- 107 - CI: `npm run format:check` is its own step.
  1061	- 108 - CI + unit: the suite runs under jsdom with Testing Library; the network stub makes "none of them touches the network" enforced rather than claimed.
  1062	- 109 - CI: coverage thresholds in `vitest.config.ts`, failing the `test:coverage` step.
  1063	- 110 - unit: a test asserting the `src/features/*/domain/**` threshold key exists in the coverage config with all four metrics at 100, so it cannot be deleted before phase 3. Its inertness today is proven by `test:coverage` passing. Vitest 4's behavior for a threshold glob matching zero files is confirmed empirically in M1 (it is configured from M1, not M3); if it errors rather than no-opping, the fallback is the post-coverage assertion script described in Risks.
  1064	- 111 - CI: `npm run build` runs `tsc -b` first.
  1065	- 112 - CI: `npm run size` is its own step and prints actual against limit for every entry of section 7.3 - 100 kB gzipped for the entry plus vendor pair, 15 kB for the stylesheet, 30 kB per route chunk, 5 kB per catalogue chunk. `build-output/size-limit-entries.test.ts` asserts `.size-limit.json` still carries those names and numbers, so a busted budget cannot be fixed by editing the budget without the edit showing up in the diff. It is a build-output test rather than a unit test - it runs under `verify:build`, not `npm test` - because it is meaningless before a `dist` exists, and an earlier draft called it a unit test while the layout placed it here. Which entries it expects is not a matter of judgement: `expected-build-output.json`'s `alwaysOn.sizeLimitEntries` holds the expected `{ name, limit }` array and the test compares `.size-limit.json` against it (section 7.1). The expectation lives in a different file from the thing it checks, which is what keeps the guard non-circular - comparing `.size-limit.json` against itself would pass any edit, defeating the whole point of the check. The array is the entry/vendor pair in M1, plus the stylesheet in M4, plus the routes and catalogues in M5, so there is exactly one correct content at each milestone. The earlier wording ("still carries those names and numbers", against a section listing seven entries) had two different correct answers at M1 and at M5, so an M1 implementer could not write it.
  1066	- 113 - CI: `npm run e2e` runs the flows listed, across the default and `development` projects.
  1067	- 114 - CI: `upload-artifact` with `if: always()`, asserted by the workflow-parse test. The one-off inspection of a deliberately failed run is a manual confirmation that the config does what it says, not a repeatable check - listed as review-dependent below rather than counted as a test.
  1068	- 115 - unit + e2e: injected clock and randomness throughout; the unit network stub; the Playwright global route handler. The discriminating part is mechanical: a lint rule bans `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `Date.now` and `new Date()` inside `src/**/*.test.*` and `e2e/**`, so a test reaching for a real timer fails lint rather than relying on nobody doing it. Injection seams alone never proved this, and the earlier entry implied they did.
  1069	- 116 - unit: the workflow-parse test asserts the `live-smoke` job's only trigger is `workflow_dispatch` and that it appears in no `needs` list.
  1070	- 116a, 116b - CI (manual): the dispatched run's log, captured to `evidence/live-smoke.txt`. The printed field names are read by a human, which is the point of the job; nothing asserts on them.
  1071	- 117 - CI: `setup-node` with `node-version-file: .nvmrc`; a unit test asserts `.nvmrc` and `package.json` `engines.node` agree.
  1072	- 118 - review: `VERIFICATION.md` and `README.md`'s command list. The workflow-parse test proves the commands exist; that they are documented where a contributor looks is a review judgement.
  1073	- 119 - review: the proof document cites runs, with evidence copied into `specs/phase-1-setup/evidence/`. Process, not a check.
  1074
  1075	### Deployment (120-126)
  1076
  1077	- 120, 121 - unit (the workflow-parse test asserts the `deploy` job's `if` condition, its `needs: verify`, and that its deploy step consumes the `site` artifact rather than running a build of its own) + CI (an actual pull-request run that does not deploy, and an actual `main` run that does). The artifact assertion is the one that discriminates: a deploy job that rebuilt would satisfy "deploys after the gates" while shipping bytes nothing verified.
  1078	- 122 - unit + e2e: a build-output test asserts every `src` and `href` in `dist/index.html` is root-relative (`/assets/...`), that no URL in `dist` carries a `/hierarchy-tree/` prefix left over from the previous hosting, and that `vite.config.ts` declares no `base` other than `/`. Static inspection cannot see a URL constructed at runtime, so the e2e half records every request the page issues (`page.on('request')`) across all routes and asserts each same-origin path resolves under `/` without a duplicated segment.
  1079	- 123 - deployed + CI: `deployed-smoke.spec.ts` against the live URL, after merge to `main`, with `DEPLOYED_BASE_URL` supplied to the `deployed` Playwright project. The CI half is the deploy job's assertion that `wrangler`'s reported `deployment-url` equals the `productionHostname` in `deployment.json` - the check that discriminates a production deployment from a preview when the Pages project's production branch was mis-set (invariant 126). A unit test additionally asserts that the hostname cited in `VERIFICATION.md` and `.env.example` matches `deployment.json`, so the documented value and the asserted value cannot diverge. Without it the smoke run tests a hostname the deploy never wrote to, and reports whatever was there before.
  1080	- 124 - deployed + script: the same spec loads `<base>/login` directly and reloads it, asserting the login placeholder both times AND that the response status is 200 - the rewrite rule serves `index.html` with a 200, so unlike the previous hosting's 404 fallback the status is part of the contract rather than something to look past. The build-output half asserts `dist/_redirects` exists and contains exactly the `/* /index.html 200` rule, so a missing or mistyped rule fails CI before any deploy.
  1081	- 125 - unit + review: the workflow-parse test asserts the deploy job's concurrency group and `cancel-in-progress: true`. That is configuration presence, not evidence that two concurrent pushes actually supersede rather than interleave - GitHub's scheduler owns the cancellation and Cloudflare owns deployment ordering, and neither is reproducible in this repository's test suite. The behavioral half is review-dependent and listed below.
  1082	- 126 - review + CI: manual, one-time setup outside the repository (the Cloudflare Pages project, its production branch set to `main`, and the two repository secrets). Named as a prerequisite in the milestone and in the pull-request description. Two of the three items diagnose themselves - a missing token or an unknown project fails the wrangler step with an explicit error - but the production-branch setting does NOT: it produces a successful upload to a preview URL. That is why invariant 123's deployment-URL assertion exists; it is the only mechanical check over any part of this invariant, and it converts the silent case into a failed job. The rest stays review-carried because it lives in a Cloudflare account no test can read.
  1083
  1084	- 126a - process: the post-merge obligation. `npm run e2e:deployed` runs against the recorded production hostname after the merge, its output is captured as `specs/phase-1-setup/evidence/deployed-smoke.txt`, and PROOF.md cites it for invariants 123 and 124. No milestone boundary and no pull-request run may mark those two as verified - M6's boundary explicitly excludes them. This is a process obligation rather than a check, and it is listed here so that "the phase is done" cannot be claimed from a green pull request alone.
  1085
  1086	### What must not be true (127-136)
  1087
  1088	- 127, 128, 129, 130 - script + lint, with the limits stated. The script matches at IDENTIFIER level, not by substring: it parses `src/**` and tests whole identifier segments against `make32`, `POISON_ARRAY`, `buildForest`, `flattenVisible`, plus string literals containing `/secrets` and the `role="tree"` attribute, with a stated allow-list for legitimate collisions (`encodeURIComponent`, `URLSearchParams`, `reportMissingKey`, `reportRootError`, `reportWebVitals`). A substring grep for `encode` and `report` - the earlier design - would have failed against the i18n and error-boundary modules this very spec requires, turning the first M3 commit red for the wrong reason. Storage access is additionally covered by the `no-restricted-globals` rule, which is the half that actually discriminates, because a grep can be defeated by renaming and the lint rule cannot be defeated by anything short of a disable comment (which `assert-no-secrets.mjs` greps for). Named honestly: these greps are a tripwire against accidental reintroduction, not a proof of absence, and they are listed below as partially review-dependent for that reason.
  1089	- 131 - unit: a test asserting `src/App.tsx`, `src/App.css`, `src/index.css`, `src/assets/` and `public/icons.svg` do not exist.
  1090	- 132 - review (see 96).
  1091	- 133 - script, in two halves that run at different times because they scan different things: `npm run lint` runs `assert-no-secrets.mjs --source-only` over `src`, and `npm run verify:build` runs `--bundle-only` over `dist` immediately after the build. The earlier single invocation inside `lint` claimed to scan `dist` while running three steps before `dist` existed, so the bundle was never scanned. `--bundle-only` FAILS on a missing `dist` rather than skipping. Both halves check: no `.env` file other than `.env.example` is tracked, no high-entropy hex or base64 literal above a length threshold, and none of `apiKey`, `authorization`, `bearer ` or a Firebase secret pattern. Entropy heuristics have false negatives by nature, which is why invariant 20's structural guarantee - nothing in configuration is secret, because the bundle is public - is the real protection and this script is the tripwire.
  1092	- 134 - unit: a test asserting `package.json`'s `dependencies` equals the expected allow-list exactly - `react`, `react-dom`, `react-router`, `zod`, `i18next`, `react-i18next`, `web-vitals`, and nothing else. A new runtime dependency fails the suite until the list is edited deliberately; `web-vitals` is on the list by the decision recorded at invariant 52, not by default.
  1093	- 135 - unit: the workflow-parse test asserts no `continue-on-error`, no `if: false`, and no skip flag on any verify step; a grep asserts no `.skip`, `.only` or `test.fixme` in `src` or `e2e`.
  1094	- 136 - review only. No mechanical check can distinguish an abstraction with no caller from a necessary seam. **Flagged as not mechanically checkable in this phase.**
  1095
  1096	### Invariants that are review-dependent
  1097
  1098	Both G1 reviewers found the earlier version of this section overstated - it listed ten invariants and then claimed "everything else has a check that fails", while several mapped checks would have passed against a broken implementation. Each of those was handled one of two ways: the check was strengthened so it discriminates (21, 32, 55, 56, 58, 59, 68, 76, 80, 86, 87, 91, 92, 99a, 100, 112, 115, 120, 122, 123, 128), or the invariant, or the specific half of it that no test reaches, was moved onto this list. The list below is the honest one. (This ledger previously cited 37 and 42, two of the retired caching invariants - a stale entry that left an auditor unable to tell whether the withdrawal had missed something. The numbers are retired, not reused, so they are simply gone from here.)
  1099
  1100	Fully review-dependent:
  1101
  1102	- 96, 96a, 132 - whether the placeholders promise nothing and carry no mockup chrome. A `lorem` grep is the only mechanical part.
  1103	- 118 - that the commands are documented where a contributor will look. The workflow-parse test proves they exist, not that they are findable.
  1104	- 119 - that the proof cites runs that happened. Process, not a check.
  1105	- 126 - the manual setup outside the repository: the Cloudflare Pages project and the two repository secrets.
  1106	- 136 - no abstraction built without a caller. No mechanical check distinguishes an unused abstraction from a necessary seam.
  1107
  1108	Partially review-dependent, with the covered half and the uncovered half named:
  1109
  1110	- 8 - the vocabulary grep covers exported names; "no domain type appears in a `shared` or `platform` signature" is review-carried in this phase, because no domain type exists yet for a check to find. It becomes mechanical in phase 3.
  1111	- 12 - the config-severity test pins the rules as errors; "argued in the decision log rather than made silently" is a review judgement about a diff.
  1112	- 102 - the workflow-parse test's command rule covers every GATING `run:` line, which is the `verify` job. The `deploy` job sits outside it by the invariant's own scoping, so its single permitted assertion (invariant 123's deployment-URL comparison) is bounded by review rather than by a test: a second `run:` line added to that job - the thing 102 says must not happen - fails nothing. Named here because this ledger claims to be the honest list, and this half of 102 became review-carried when the deploy job's assertion was admitted.
  1113	- 64 - the `no-restricted-syntax` rule bans the `toLocale*` methods; that `Intl` is used correctly is unobservable until phase 3 formats something.
  1114	- 72 - the contrast test walks `contrastPairs.ts` and fails on any listed pair below AA. That the list covers the pairs components actually use is review-carried; a component using an unlisted pair is caught by a reviewer, not by the test.
  1115	- 114 - the workflow-parse test asserts `if: always()`. The one-off inspection of a genuinely failed run is a manual confirmation, not a repeatable check.
  1116	- 125 - the workflow-parse test asserts the concurrency group and `cancel-in-progress`. That two concurrent pushes actually supersede is GitHub scheduler behavior, not reproducible here.
  1117	- 127, 128, 129, 130 - the identifier-level script plus the storage lint rules are a tripwire against accidental reintroduction. A determined rename or a constructed string defeats the script; the lint rules and the absence of any repository module are the load-bearing parts. For 128 specifically, the identifier-and-member ban plus the e2e storage-emptiness assertion (section 2.4) covers the static and the observable-effect case; a write performed through a computed member access on a storage global is caught only if it actually writes, which the e2e assertion sees and lint cannot.
  1118
  1119	- File and module naming conventions (section 1) - review only, and declared non-binding there. No lint rule, script or structural test checks filenames, barrels, named exports or `memo` usage, so a kebab-case module or an unmemoized component passes the whole pipeline. The one case where a name is load-bearing rather than stylistic - the emitted route chunk names the `size-limit` globs and invariant 89's assertions are written against - is covered mechanically by those globs failing on no match, which does not depend on the convention being honoured.
  1120	- 133 - entropy and pattern heuristics have false negatives by nature. Invariant 20's structural guarantee is the real protection.
  1121
  1122	For everything not named in this section, the mapping above names a check intended to fail against a broken implementation. That is a design intent stated per invariant, not a blanket guarantee: the previous two versions of this sentence claimed more than the map delivered, and a reviewer should treat any individual entry as a claim to be checked rather than as a certification. Where an entry's check turns out not to discriminate once the code exists, the honest response is to strengthen it or move the invariant onto this list, not to leave the sentence standing.
  1123
  1124	## Risks and mitigations
  1125
  1126	- **The entry budget is a set number, not a measured one, until M1 builds.** 100 kB gzipped was set against an estimate of 85-90 kB for the FIXED RUNTIME DEPENDENCY SET ALONE - the reading ARCHITECTURE.md's decision log and PRODUCT.md invariant 112 both state, and the one section 7.3 settles on. The budget MEASURES the entry plus vendor pair, which is that dependency set plus the app's own shell, kit and platform code, so the real headroom is 100 kB minus 85-90 kB minus whatever the app weighs - thinner than the raw numbers suggest, and shrinking as phases 2 and 3 add code. react-dom alone is roughly 45 kB gzipped; react-router, i18next with react-i18next and Zod carry most of the rest; `web-vitals` adds about 3 kB. Because the pair includes the app's own shell, kit and platform code, the nominal 10-15% headroom is thinner than a dependencies-only reading suggests, and it shrinks as phases 2 and 3 add code. The first real measurement is now the `npm run size` step in M1 rather than M6, so a bust surfaces before five milestones are built on the assumption; if the estimate was wrong, the number is revisited with the user rather than silently raised. Three things the implementation does anyway to keep the entry small, none of them an escape hatch: import `zod/mini` in the configuration schema (Zod 4 ships a tree-shakable variant), import i18next and react-i18next through their ESM entries so unused plugins drop, and keep anything a route can own out of the entry. The one structural move held in reserve - putting i18next initialization behind the first route chunk - weakens invariant 62's guarantee and would be a decision-log change, not a quiet fix.
  1127	- **Framing protection now depends on a file no local run can exercise.** The conflict between invariant 99 (the CSP directive list) and invariant 100 (an empty console) is resolved in PRODUCT.md: `frame-ancestors` is no longer part of the meta policy, because a meta-tag CSP ignores it and browsers warn about it. It moved to `public/_headers`, which the new hosting serves as a real response header (invariant 99a) - so the exposure the previous hosting left permanently open is closed. The residual risk is different in kind and worth naming: `vite preview` sets no headers, so nothing in the local suite or in CI proves the header is actually served. The build-output test can only assert the file's content. It now asserts that content EXACTLY rather than by containment (invariant 99a), which closes two holes an earlier draft left open - a mis-indented header line, which Cloudflare silently ignores while a containment check passes, and a later edit adding directives, which would recreate the two-disagreeing-policies mode the split exists to prevent. What exactness still cannot catch is a path pattern that is well-formed but matches nothing in practice. The deployed smoke run reading the live response headers is the only real check for that, and it runs after merge under the obligation of invariant 126a.
  1128	- **`web-vitals` is a runtime dependency added against invariant 134's default.** It is on the allow-list by decision: `PerformanceObserver` gives the maximum interaction latency and a running layout-shift sum cheaply, and neither is the metric it would have been labelled as - INP is a high percentile of interaction latencies under a specific windowing rule, CLS is the session-window maximum. Shipping approximations under the names `INP` and `CLS` would make the telemetry lie. The cost is one more package in the entry: version 6.1.0, standard build, 8,963 bytes raw and about 3.3 kB gzipped for the whole module, less after tree-shaking to `onLCP`/`onINP`/`onCLS`; the `attribution` build is deliberately not used. The dependency allow-list test of invariant 134 is what keeps this one deliberate addition from becoming a precedent.
  1129	- **`eslint-plugin-i18next` false positives against Tailwind.** With `mode: 'all'`, every `className` string is reported. The configuration is `mode: 'jsx-only'` with an explicit `ignoreAttribute` list (`className`, `data-testid`, `role`, `type`, `id`, `name`, `href`, `rel`, `referrerPolicy`, `loading`, `width`, `height`, `autoComplete`, `dir`, `lang`), which keeps `aria-label`, `alt` and `title` checked - the attributes that are actually user-visible. The risk is maintenance: a new non-visible attribute produces a false positive and the reflex is to add an inline disable. The mitigation is that the ignore list is a reviewed edit in one place and the suppression grep in `assert-no-secrets.mjs` makes an inline disable visible.
  1130	- **`eslint-plugin-boundaries` configuration drift.** The plugin fails open in one specific way: if the `boundaries/elements` pattern stops matching a file (a directory rename, a new nesting level), the file becomes unknown rather than unrestricted - which is why `boundaries/no-unknown-files` is set to error. That converts the fail-open mode into a loud failure. The residual risk is a pattern that matches the wrong element (for example a nested `src/features/auth/features/` directory), which the two evidence captures would not catch. Mitigation: the M2 evidence run injects violations in both directions, and the config-severity unit test pins the rules as errors.
     1	# Architecture
     2
     3	Technical decisions behind [GOAL.md](./GOAL.md). High level by design: it states what exists and why, not how each file is written. Implementation detail belongs to task decomposition.
     4
     5	## 1. Context and constraints
     6
     7	- The backend is fixed and cannot be changed: a public Firebase REST database with a flat `users` collection and a `secrets` map of secret to user id. There is no session endpoint, no pagination, no filtering.
     8	- The dataset is small (33 users, ~9KB) and the payload is public, including plaintext passwords.
     9	- Client-only static hosting. There is no server we own, so anything a backend would normally do is either mitigated in the client or documented as a gap.
    10	- The app must stay small enough to read in one sitting while still carrying the concerns a production app carries: observability, i18n, accessibility, resilience, testing, budgets.
    11
    12	The guiding rule: **the brief bounds the features, not the engineering.** Nothing is built that GOAL.md does not ask for; the depth goes into how the requested behavior is built.
    13
    14	## 2. System overview
    15
    16	Four layers with one-directional imports. Features never reach into each other, and the platform never knows what a "user" is.
    17
    18	```mermaid
    19	graph TD
    20	    app["app<br/>router, providers, boundaries"]
    21	    auth["features/auth<br/>login, session, guard"]
    22	    hierarchy["features/hierarchy<br/>tree domain, tree UI"]
    23	    shared["shared<br/>UI primitives, hooks, test utils"]
    24	    platform["platform<br/>http, config, observability, i18n"]
    25
    26	    app --> auth
    27	    app --> hierarchy
    28	    auth --> shared
    29	    auth --> platform
    30	    hierarchy --> shared
    31	    hierarchy --> platform
    32	    shared --> platform
    33	    auth -. forbidden .-> hierarchy
    34	```
    35
    36	- `app` owns composition: the router, the provider stack, the root error boundary. It is the only place that knows the full feature set.
    37	- `features/*` own a slice end to end - route module, data access, domain logic, components - and expose a single public entry. Everything else is internal.
    38	- `shared` holds framework-level building blocks with no domain knowledge.
    39	- `platform` holds adapters to the outside world: HTTP, configuration, logging/tracing/analytics, i18n. Swappable without touching features.
    40
    41	The rules are enforced, not documented: `eslint-plugin-boundaries` plus `no-restricted-imports` fail CI on a cross-feature or deep import.
    42
    43	Routing runs in React Router library mode (`createBrowserRouter`) so Vite stays the only build tool and the output remains static files. Route modules are lazily imported, which makes the route boundary the code-splitting boundary.
    44
    45	## 3. Runtime flow
    46
    47	```mermaid
    48	sequenceDiagram
    49	    participant U as User
    50	    participant R as Router
    51	    participant A as auth
    52	    participant H as http
    53	    participant F as Firebase
    54
    55	    U->>A: submit email + password (useActionState)
    56	    A->>A: encode(email, password) -> secret
    57	    A->>H: GET /secrets/{secret}.json
    58	    H->>F: fetch (traceparent, timeout, retry)
    59	    F-->>A: userId | null
    60	    A->>A: null -> field-level error, stay on /login
    61	    A->>R: persist session, navigate to `from` or /
    62	    R->>H: hierarchy loader starts users fetch (not awaited)
    63	    R->>U: route renders, Suspense shows skeleton
    64	    H-->>R: validated users
    65	    R->>U: use(promise) resolves, forest renders
    66	```
    67
    68	Two properties matter here. The loader starts the request at navigation time, so there is no render-then-fetch waterfall. And the login lookup fetches only `/secrets/{secret}.json` - the app never downloads the password table to authenticate.
    69
    70	## 4. Cross-cutting concerns
    71
    72	### Data access
    73
    74	A single `http` client owns every network call: base URL from config, `AbortController` timeout, one bounded exponential-backoff-with-jitter retry for idempotent GETs only (never on 4xx), trace header propagation, and timing telemetry. Its transport is injected, which is what makes component tests possible without a mock server.
    75
    76	Above it, a repository per resource maps raw JSON to domain types. The router's loader starts the request at navigation time and the component reads the returned promise with `use()`, so a resource has exactly one fetch site.
    77
    78	There is no response cache in this roadmap. Request dedupe, TTL and stale-while-revalidate are **withdrawn, not deferred** - they are outside this roadmap entirely, and reinstating them is a new decision-log entry rather than scheduled work (see the decision log). Each navigation that needs the users payload fetches it, which at 33 users and ~9KB is a request the app can afford, and the repository is the seam a cache attaches to when one is worth its complexity.
    79
    80	No data-fetching library. React 19 primitives (`use`, Suspense, transitions, `useActionState`) plus the router's loader/action lifecycle cover what this app needs.
    81
    82	### Domain model
    83
    84	Tree construction is pure, framework-free, and the most heavily tested code in the repo:
    85
    86	- `buildForest(users)` - O(n) grouping by `managerId`. Users with no manager, a dangling `managerId`, or a cycle become roots; cycles are broken and reported to telemetry rather than hanging the render.
    87	- `flattenVisible(forest, expandedIds)` - produces the visible row list with `depth`, `hasChildren`, `isExpanded`, `setSize`, `posInSet`. This shape serves the ARIA attributes, the render, and any future virtualizer.
    88
    89	The UI renders that row list with memoized rows keyed by user id. Nothing in the domain layer imports React.
    90
    91	### Validation and error taxonomy
    92
    93	Zod schemas validate at the API boundary. Parsing is tolerant per row: an invalid user is dropped and counted in telemetry instead of failing the page, because a shared public database can change under us. Ids and emails are branded types, so a raw number cannot be passed where a user id is expected.
    94
    95	Failures are a small typed union - `NetworkError`, `TimeoutError`, `HttpError(status)`, `ParseError` - mapped once in the http client. The UI has four states everywhere data is involved: skeleton, error with a retry that re-runs the loader, empty, and data.
    96
    97	### Accessibility
    98
    99	The tree implements the full WAI-ARIA tree pattern, not a nested list with buttons: `role=tree` / `treeitem` / `group`, roving tabindex so the whole tree is one tab stop, arrow keys to move and expand/collapse, Home/End, type-ahead, and `aria-expanded` / `aria-level` / `aria-setsize` / `aria-posinset` from the flattened row model. Expand/collapse changes are announced through a live region.
   100
   101	Beyond the widget: visible focus rings, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected, color contrast held to WCAG AA in both themes, avatars carrying meaningful alternatives and falling back to initials. `jsx-a11y` lints the markup, axe-core asserts on rendered components in unit tests, and `@axe-core/playwright` asserts on real pages in e2e - the a11y claim is enforced in CI rather than asserted in a README.
   102
   103	### Internationalization
   104
   105	i18next with a namespace per feature, lazy-loaded with the route. Every user-visible string lives in a catalogue; `eslint-plugin-i18next` fails the build on hardcoded literals. Dates, numbers, names and lists format through `Intl`, never string concatenation.
   106
   107	English ships alone, but the pipeline is exercised end to end so a second locale is a content change, not a refactor. Layout uses logical properties (`padding-inline-start` for tree indentation, `text-start`, `ms-*`/`ps-*` utilities) throughout, so an RTL locale needs a catalogue and a `dir` switch, nothing more.
   108
   109	### Observability
   110
   111	One facade in `platform/observability` exposing three narrow interfaces - logger, tracer, analytics - over swappable sinks: console in development, an in-memory ring buffer in production builds, no-op in tests unless asserted on. A vendor SDK is a one-line sink swap.
   112
   113	- Every request gets a W3C `traceparent`; the same correlation id appears on the request log, on any error the boundary reports, and on the analytics event for that interaction.
   114	- Analytics events are a typed union with a documented catalogue, so event names are refactorable and cannot drift.
   115	- Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) are collected through the `web-vitals` package and reported through the same facade. This reverses an earlier "no dependency" position; see the decision log.
   116	- A redaction layer scrubs `password`, `secret` and `token` keys before anything reaches a sink.
   117
   118	E2E asserts against the buffer sink, which makes the telemetry contract a tested behavior rather than decoration.
   119
   120	### Performance and budgets
   121
   122	- Route-level code splitting; the login route never pays for the tree route.
   123	- The forest is built once per payload and memoized; toggling a node recomputes only the visible row list.
   124	- Rows are memoized components keyed by id. Virtualization is deliberately not shipped for 33 rows, but `flattenVisible` already produces exactly what a windowing layer consumes - the seam is named and the threshold documented (~500 visible rows).
   125	- Avatars are lazily loaded with explicit dimensions to avoid layout shift, and fall back to initials on error.
   126	- Budgets are numbers in the repo, checked by `size-limit` in CI: app entry and per-route chunk ceilings in gzipped kB. Field targets: LCP under 1.5s and INP under 200ms on a mid-tier device.
   127
   128	### Security posture
   129
   130	The constraint is that client-side auth is not authentication. What we control, we do:
   131
   132	- Only `/secrets/{secret}.json` is fetched at login; the users table with its plaintext passwords is never pulled for authentication.
   133	- Secrets and passwords never enter URLs, logs, telemetry or storage. The session record holds a user id and a schema version, in `sessionStorage`, scoped to the tab.
   134	- A CSP meta tag constrains sources; third-party avatar URLs load with `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`. The meta tag carries no `frame-ancestors` directive, because browsers ignore it there. Framing protection needs a response header, and Cloudflare Pages sets one from a `_headers` file in the build output. See the decision log.
   135	- Route guards run in loaders (redirect with a `from` param), not in render, so an unauthenticated user never triggers a data fetch.
   136
   137	The gap is stated plainly in the code and in this document: a real deployment puts a BFF in front of this, which performs the lookup server-side and issues an httpOnly session cookie. The auth module isolates that seam so replacing it touches one file.
   138
   139	### UI and UX
   140
   141	Tailwind v4 with a CSS-first theme, so design tokens - color, spacing, type scale, radii, motion - are declared once and consumed as utilities. Dark mode via `prefers-color-scheme`, layout responsive from 320px up with container queries on tree rows so deep nesting stays usable on narrow screens.
   142
   143	Expand/collapse state lives in a URL search param: the view is shareable, the back button works, and a refresh preserves the shape of the tree. On first paint, roots and their first level are expanded so the org shape is immediately legible.
   144
   145	## 5. Quality pipeline
   146
   147	- **Types**: TypeScript strict, no `any`, no non-null assertions; type-aware ESLint rules (`recommendedTypeChecked`) so lint sees types.
   148	- **Lint**: ESLint owns correctness and architecture - boundaries, `jsx-a11y`, `react-hooks`, `i18next` literals, testing-library and Playwright hygiene. Prettier owns formatting, with Tailwind class sorting; `eslint-config-prettier` keeps them from overlapping.
   149	- **Unit and component**: Vitest with jsdom and Testing Library. The pure domain is held at ~100%; components are tested by behavior and keyboard contract, with axe assertions. Component tests inject a fake transport fed from the same fixtures the e2e mocks serve.
   150	- **E2E**: Playwright with `route()` mocks by default - deterministic, offline-capable, and able to exercise failure paths (500, timeout, empty payload, malformed row, cycle) that a live API will not produce on demand. A separate script runs smoke tests against the real database to catch contract drift; it never gates the default suite.
   151	- **CI**: one GitHub Actions workflow on PR and main - typecheck, lint and format check, unit tests with coverage thresholds, build, size budgets, e2e with report artifact. A manually triggered job runs the live smoke tests.
   152	- **Deploy**: main deploys to Cloudflare Pages from the same workflow, after every gate has passed, so review starts with a URL rather than an install.
   153	- **Config**: a single typed module reads `import.meta.env` once, validates at startup, and exposes environment-shaped defaults (API base URL, log level, sink, feature flags). No `import.meta.env` reads scattered through the code.
   154
   155	## 6. Decision log
   156
   157	Each entry: the choice, why, and what was rejected.
   158
   159	- **React Router library mode over framework mode** - keeps Vite the only build tool and the output static, which matches the hosting constraint. Framework mode brings routing machinery, typegen and a server story this app never uses.
   160	- **Loader starts the fetch, `use()` suspends, over a blocking loader** - removes the render-then-fetch waterfall while keeping granular skeletons. A blocking loader is simpler but gives up streaming; pure Suspense without loaders reintroduces the waterfall.
   161	- **No response cache in this roadmap** (2026-08-13, phase 1) - the earlier position was an own cache module over TanStack Query, on the grounds that dedupe, TTL and stale-while-revalidate are small enough to own. Specifying it proved otherwise: the state machine, per-key generations, revalidation cooldowns and their tests were the largest single piece of the phase 1 spec, and it exists to save one 9KB request on a dataset of 33 users. The cache is withdrawn from the roadmap, not designed and deferred - phases 1 to 3 ship without it and the repository per resource is the seam it attaches to afterwards. Rejected: TanStack Query, which is the same weight bought rather than written; and keeping the module in phase 3, which would land a cache and the tree domain in one loop. The withdrawn design is kept whole in [CACHE.md](./CACHE.md), including the ten review findings it absorbed, so reinstating it is a decision rather than a rewrite.
   162	- **Zod at the boundary over hand-written guards** - the schemas are the parsing rules, the types, and the documentation in one place, and per-row `safeParse` gives tolerant parsing cheaply. Hand-written guards avoid a dependency but drift from the types they protect.
   163	- **Feature-sliced with lint-enforced boundaries over layer-by-type** - a feature's code stays in one place, and the boundary is a CI failure rather than a convention. Rejected a workspaces monorepo as tooling cost out of proportion to the app.
   164	- **Full ARIA tree widget over nested lists with disclosure buttons** - the brief describes a tree; the accessible tree has a defined keyboard contract, and claiming the role without the contract is worse than not claiming it. The list version is simpler but turns 33 users into 33 tab stops.
   165	- **`sessionStorage` user id over in-memory or `localStorage`** - survives reload, dies with the tab, and stores nothing sensitive. In-memory reads as a bug on refresh; `localStorage` widens exposure of something standing in for a credential.
   166	- **Playwright route mocks over a shared mock server** - one browser-level mocking mechanism, no extra dependency, and full control over failure injection. Live coverage is preserved through a separate, explicitly run smoke suite.
   167	- **Tailwind v4 over CSS Modules with tokens** - the theme layer gives a real token system and the utility layer keeps styling decisions visible in the component, with class ordering enforced by Prettier.
   168	- **English-only i18n with full infrastructure** - the pipeline is what is expensive to retrofit; a second catalogue is not. Shipping a token second locale would prove less than exercising the real one.
   169	- **`web-vitals` as a dependency over hand-rolled `PerformanceObserver` collection** (2026-08-13, phase 1) - INP is a high percentile of interaction latencies under a specific windowing rule, and CLS is a session-window maximum. `PerformanceObserver` cheaply yields a maximum interaction latency and a running shift sum, which are different numbers. Reporting those under the labels `INP` and `CLS` would make the telemetry lie about what it measures, and the facade's whole point is that the contract is tested rather than asserted. Rejected: shipping the approximations under honest alternative names, which keeps the dependency count at zero but leaves the app with no comparable field metric; and dropping INP and CLS entirely, which gives up the interaction budget the performance section commits to. The cost is one small runtime dependency inside the entry budget.
   170	- **No `frame-ancestors` in the CSP meta tag; the response header instead** (2026-08-13, phase 1) - browsers ignore `frame-ancestors` when it arrives in a meta tag and log a warning saying so, so including it would buy no protection while producing a permanent console warning, forcing an allow-list entry into the e2e console assertion that otherwise stays empty. Rejected: keeping the directive in the meta tag as a statement of intent. Framing protection therefore ships as a response header, which Cloudflare Pages sets from a `_headers` file in the build output - the one thing the previous hosting choice could not do. Everything else stays in the meta tag, so there is one policy to read rather than two half-policies.
   171	- **Cloudflare Pages over GitHub Pages** (2026-08-13, phase 1) - the repository is private, and GitHub Pages does not serve a site from a private repository on this account's plan, so the hosting decision had to be remade rather than debated. Cloudflare Pages serves the site at the root (no project sub-path, so the Vite `base` stays `/`), gives SPA deep links through a `_redirects` rule instead of a `404.html` copy, and sets response headers from `_headers`, which is what makes framing protection possible at all. Deployment stays inside the same GitHub Actions workflow, running `wrangler pages deploy` after every gate has passed, so the rule that a deploy follows a green pipeline is unchanged. Rejected: Cloudflare's own Git integration, which builds and deploys on push without waiting for the workflow's gates, giving up exactly that property; and making the repository public to keep Pages, which is not a hosting decision.
   172	- **App entry budget of 100 kB gzipped** (2026-08-13, phase 1) - set against an estimate of 85-90 kB for the fixed dependency set (react-dom, react-router, zod, i18next, react-i18next, web-vitals), leaving roughly 10-15% headroom. Rejected: 75 kB, which the dependency set alone would likely bust, turning the budget into noise the first time it ran; and deferring the number until measured, which leaves CI with no size gate while the skeleton is built. Per-route chunks stay at 30 kB.
   173	- **App entry budget revised to 150 kB gzipped** (2026-08-13, phase 1) - wiring the real router in M5 step 31 measured the entry at 112.77 kB, busting the 100 kB budget by 12.77 kB. An isolated esbuild probe (`createBrowserRouter` + `RouterProvider` alone, tree-shaken, react/react-dom externalized) put react-router's own weight at ~31 kB gzipped - the original 85-90 kB estimate undercounted react-router specifically, this was not a tree-shaking regression or a code defect. Per this section's own rule, a wrong estimate is revisited with the user rather than silently raised; the user set the corrected number at 150 kB, leaving headroom over the measured 112.77 kB rather than pinning the limit to the exact current build. Rejected: a code-splitting mitigation to defer router construction, which was not pursued because the router must exist to render the very first route - there is no idle window before it that deferral could exploit.
   174	- **Two design tokens darkened past their mockup literals: `border-field` and `ink-faint`** (2026-08-13, phase 1) - `docs/reference.md`'s pulled values (`#E2DDEE` field border, `#8E8AA0` faint ink) hold 1.33:1 and 3.34:1/4.31:1 (light/dark) against the surfaces they sit on, both short of invariant 72's AA floor (3:1 for UI boundaries, 4.5:1 for body text - the correlation id `ErrorState` renders in `ink-faint`, per invariant 92, is body text). `theme.css` re-declares both tokens (`border-field` `#8F89A3`, `ink-faint` `#726E85` light / `#847F95` dark) with `contrastPairs.test.ts` entries proving the new values clear AA in both themes. Rejected: keeping the mockup literals and accepting the AA failure, which invariant 70's mockup-fidelity goal does not outrank invariant 72's binding accessibility floor; and reusing an existing darker token (`ink-muted`) for the correlation id instead of darkening `ink-faint`, which would collapse two intentionally distinct text weights into one.
   175
   176	## 7. Deliberately not built
   177
   178	Named so the omissions read as decisions, with the seam that makes each cheap later:
   179
   180	- **Virtualized rendering** - unnecessary at 33 rows; `flattenVisible` already emits the row model a windowing layer needs.
   181	- **Real auth** - impossible against this API from a static client; `features/auth` isolates the lookup so a BFF-issued cookie replaces one module.
   182	- **Offline / service worker** - a 9KB public payload does not justify a cache lifecycle; the repository layer is where a persistent cache would attach.
   183	- **Response caching** - dedupe, TTL and stale-while-revalidate, withdrawn from the roadmap by the decision log entry above; the design is preserved in [CACHE.md](./CACHE.md). The repository per resource is the seam: caching attaches behind it without a caller changing.
   184	- **Search, filtering, org editing** - outside GOAL.md. The tree domain is pure and already returns the row model a filter would narrow.
   185	- **A second locale, SSR, a component library** - infrastructure supports each; none is needed to satisfy the goal.
   186	- **Vendor telemetry** - the facade defines the contract; a real sink is a swap, not a rewrite.

    15	export type HttpClientDependencies = {
    16	  transport: Transport;
    17	  clock: Clock;
    18	  randomness: Randomness;
    19	  observability: ObservabilityFacade;
    20	  configuration: Pick<
    21	    Configuration,

    23	  >;
    24	  // The interaction tracker's currentCorrelationId() (invariant 47) - the
    25	  // trace id sent on the wire and the timing record's correlationId are
    26	  // both this value, not the per-logical-request requestId below, which
    27	  // only ties a request's own retried attempts together.

    31	export type HttpClient = {
    32	  request<Value>(request: HttpRequest<Value>): Promise<HttpResult<Value>>;
    33	};
    34
    35	const MAXIMUM_RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 1;
    36
    37	type AttemptOutcome<Value> =
    38	  | { kind: 'success'; value: Value; status: number }
    39	  | { kind: 'failure'; failure: HttpFailure }
    40	  | { kind: 'aborted' };
    41
    42	export function createHttpClient(
    43	  dependencies: HttpClientDependencies,
    44	): HttpClient {
    45	  const {
    46	    transport,
    47	    clock,
    48	    randomness,
    49	    observability,
    50	    configuration,
    51	    correlationId: getCorrelationId,
    52	  } = dependencies;
    53
    54	  async function request<Value>(
    55	    httpRequest: HttpRequest<Value>,
    56	  ): Promise<HttpResult<Value>> {
    57	    if (httpRequest.resourcePath.startsWith('//')) {
    58	      observability.logger.error('http.invalid_resource_path', {
    59	        resourcePath: httpRequest.resourcePath,
    60	      });
    61	      return { outcome: 'failure', failure: { kind: 'network' } };
    62	    }
    63
    64	    if (httpRequest.signal?.aborted) {
    65	      return { outcome: 'cancelled' };
    66	    }
    67
    68	    const requestId = createCorrelationId(randomness);
    69	    const correlationId = getCorrelationId();
    70	    const timeoutMilliseconds =
    71	      httpRequest.timeoutMilliseconds ??
    72	      configuration.requestTimeoutMilliseconds;
    73	    const deadlineController = new AbortController();
    74	    const cancelDeadlineTimer = clock.setTimer(timeoutMilliseconds, () => {
    75	      deadlineController.abort();
    76	    });
    77	    const signal = httpRequest.signal
    78	      ? AbortSignal.any([httpRequest.signal, deadlineController.signal])
    79	      : deadlineController.signal;
    80
    81	    try {
    82	      let attempt = 0;
    83
    84	      while (true) {
    85	        const attemptStartedAt = clock.now();
    86	        const traceparent = createTraceparent(correlationId, randomness);
    87	        const url = buildUrl(configuration.apiBaseUrl, httpRequest);
    88	        const rawOutcome = await performAttempt(
    89	          httpRequest,
    90	          url,
    91	          traceparent,
    92	          signal,
    93	          transport,
    94	        );
    95	        const durationMilliseconds = clock.now() - attemptStartedAt;
    96
    97	        if (rawOutcome.kind === 'aborted') {
    98	          if (httpRequest.signal?.aborted) {
    99	            observability.logger.debug('http.request_cancelled', {
   100	              resourcePath: httpRequest.resourcePath,
   101	              requestId,
   102	            });
   103	            return { outcome: 'cancelled' };
   104	          }
   105
   106	          observability.tracer.recordTiming({
   107	            method: httpRequest.method,
   108	            resourcePath: httpRequest.resourcePath,
   109	            outcome: 'failure',
   110	            durationMilliseconds,
   111	            correlationId,
   112	            attempt,
   113	            requestId,
   114	          });
   115	          return {
   116	            outcome: 'failure',
   117	            failure: { kind: 'timeout', timeoutMilliseconds },
   118	          };
   119	        }
   120
   121	        const status =
   122	          rawOutcome.kind === 'success'
   123	            ? rawOutcome.status
   124	            : rawOutcome.failure.kind === 'http'
   125	              ? rawOutcome.failure.status
   126	              : undefined;
   127	        observability.tracer.recordTiming({
   128	          method: httpRequest.method,
   129	          resourcePath: httpRequest.resourcePath,
   130	          outcome: rawOutcome.kind,
   131	          durationMilliseconds,
   132	          correlationId,
   133	          attempt,
   134	          requestId,
   135	          ...(status !== undefined ? { status } : {}),
   136	        });
   137
   138	        if (rawOutcome.kind === 'success') {
   139	          return {
   140	            outcome: 'success',
   141	            value: rawOutcome.value,
   142	            status: rawOutcome.status,
   143	          };
   144	        }
   145
   146	        if (
   147	          attempt < MAXIMUM_RETRY_ATTEMPTS &&
   148	          shouldRetry(attempt, httpRequest.method, rawOutcome.failure)
   149	        ) {
   150	          const delay = retryDelayMilliseconds(
   151	            attempt,
   152	            randomness.nextUnitInterval(),
   153	          );
   154	          try {
   155	            await clock.wait(delay, signal);
   156	          } catch {
   157	            if (httpRequest.signal?.aborted) return { outcome: 'cancelled' };
   158	            return {
   159	              outcome: 'failure',
   160	              failure: { kind: 'timeout', timeoutMilliseconds },
   161	            };
   162	          }
   163	          attempt += 1;
   164	          continue;
   165	        }
   166
   167	        return { outcome: 'failure', failure: rawOutcome.failure };
   168	      }
   169	    } finally {
   170	      cancelDeadlineTimer();
   171	    }
   172	  }
   173
   174	  return { request };
   175	}
   176
   177	function buildUrl(
   178	  apiBaseUrl: string,
   179	  httpRequest: HttpRequest<unknown>,
   180	): string {
   181	  const url = new URL(httpRequest.resourcePath, apiBaseUrl);
   182	  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(
   183	    httpRequest.searchParameters ?? {},
   184	  )) {
   185	    url.searchParams.set(key, value);
   186	  }
   187	  return url.toString();
   188	}
   189
   190	function statusDescription(status: number): string {
   191	  if (status >= 500) return 'server error';
   192	  if (status >= 400) return 'client error';
   193	  return 'error';
   194	}
   195
   196	async function performAttempt<Value>(
   197	  httpRequest: HttpRequest<Value>,
   198	  url: string,
   199	  traceparent: string,
   200	  signal: AbortSignal,
   201	  transport: Transport,
   202	): Promise<AttemptOutcome<Value>> {
   203	  const headers = new Headers({ traceparent });
   204	  let body: BodyInit | undefined;
   205	  if (httpRequest.body !== undefined) {
   206	    headers.set('content-type', 'application/json');
   207	    body = JSON.stringify(httpRequest.body);
   208	  }
   209	  const webRequest = new Request(url, {
   210	    method: httpRequest.method,
   211	    headers,
   212	    signal,
   213	    ...(body !== undefined ? { body } : {}),
   214	  });
   215
   216	  let response: Response;
   217	  try {
   218	    response = await transport(webRequest);
   219	  } catch {
   220	    if (signal.aborted) return { kind: 'aborted' };
   221	    return { kind: 'failure', failure: { kind: 'network' } };
   222	  }
   223
   224	  if (!response.ok) {
   225	    return {
   226	      kind: 'failure',
   227	      failure: {
   228	        kind: 'http',
   229	        status: response.status,
   230	        statusDescription: statusDescription(response.status),
   231	      },
   232	    };
   233	  }
   234
   235	  try {
   236	    const payload: unknown = await response.json();
   237	    return {
   238	      kind: 'success',
   239	      value: httpRequest.parse(payload),
   240	      status: response.status,
   241	    };
   242	  } catch {
   243	    return { kind: 'failure', failure: { kind: 'parse' } };
   244	  }
   245	}

    20	function createHangingTransport(): {
    21	  transport: Transport;
    22	  callCount: () => number;
    23	} {
    24	  let calls = 0;
    25	  const transport: Transport = (request) => {
    26	    calls += 1;
    27	    return new Promise((_resolve, reject) => {
    28	      request.signal.addEventListener('abort', () => {
    29	        reject(new DOMException('aborted', 'AbortError'));
    30	      });
    31	    });
    32	  };
    33	  return { transport, callCount: () => calls };
    34	}

     1	import type { HttpFailure } from './httpFailure';
     2	import type { HttpRequest } from './httpRequest';
     3
     4	const MAXIMUM_RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 1;
     5	const RETRYABLE_FAILURE_KINDS = new Set<HttpFailure['kind']>([
     6	  'network',
     7	  'timeout',
     8	]);
     9
    10	export function shouldRetry(
    11	  attempt: number,
    12	  method: HttpRequest<unknown>['method'],
    13	  failure: HttpFailure,
    14	): boolean {
    15	  if (attempt >= MAXIMUM_RETRY_ATTEMPTS) return false;
    16	  if (method !== 'GET') return false;
    17	  if (failure.kind === 'http') return failure.status >= 500;
    18	  return RETRYABLE_FAILURE_KINDS.has(failure.kind);
    19	}
     1	const BASE_DELAY_MILLISECONDS = 200;
     2	const MAXIMUM_DELAY_MILLISECONDS = 2000;
     3
     4	export function retryDelayMilliseconds(
     5	  attempt: number,
     6	  randomUnitInterval: number,
     7	): number {
     8	  const exponentialDelay = Math.min(
     9	    MAXIMUM_DELAY_MILLISECONDS,
    10	    BASE_DELAY_MILLISECONDS * 2 ** attempt,
    11	  );
    12	  return exponentialDelay * (0.5 + 0.5 * randomUnitInterval);
    13	}

     7	export function createTraceparent(
     8	  traceId: string,
     9	  randomness: Randomness,
    10	): string {

    15	function bytesToHex(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
    16	  return Array.from(bytes, (byte) => byte.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join(
    17	    '',
    18	  );

     1	const REDACTED_PLACEHOLDER = '[redacted]';
     2	const REDACTED_KEY_PATTERN = /password|secret|token/i;
     3	const CIRCULAR_PLACEHOLDER = '[circular]';
     4
     5	export function redact<Value>(value: Value): Value {
     6	  return redactValue(value, new WeakSet()) as Value;
     7	}
     8
     9	function redactValue(value: unknown, seen: WeakSet<object>): unknown {
    10	  if (typeof value === 'string') {
    11	    return redactUrlSearchParameters(value);
    12	  }
    13
    14	  if (Array.isArray(value)) {
    15	    if (seen.has(value)) return CIRCULAR_PLACEHOLDER;
    16	    seen.add(value);
    17	    // Removed on the way back out: `seen` tracks the current recursion
    18	    // PATH (ancestors), not every object visited so far - otherwise the
    19	    // same object reachable twice via two sibling branches (a DAG, not a
    20	    // cycle) would be wrongly flagged circular on its second occurrence.
    21	    const result = value.map((item) => redactValue(item, seen));
    22	    seen.delete(value);
    23	    return result;
    24	  }
    25
    26	  if (value !== null && typeof value === 'object') {
    27	    if (seen.has(value)) return CIRCULAR_PLACEHOLDER;
    28	    seen.add(value);
    29	    const source = value as Record<string, unknown>;
    30	    const result: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    31	    for (const key of Object.keys(source)) {
    32	      result[key] = REDACTED_KEY_PATTERN.test(key)
    33	        ? REDACTED_PLACEHOLDER
    34	        : redactValue(source[key], seen);
    35	    }
    36	    seen.delete(value);
    37	    return result;
    38	  }
    39
    40	  return value;
    41	}
    42
    43	function redactUrlSearchParameters(value: string): string {
    44	  let url: URL;
    45	  try {
    46	    url = new URL(value);
    47	  } catch {
    48	    return value;
    49	  }
    50
    51	  let redacted = false;
    52	  for (const key of [...url.searchParams.keys()]) {
    53	    if (REDACTED_KEY_PATTERN.test(key)) {
    54	      url.searchParams.set(key, REDACTED_PLACEHOLDER);
    55	      redacted = true;
    56	    }
    57	  }
    58
    59	  return redacted ? url.toString() : value;
    60	}

     1	import type { Configuration } from '@platform/configuration';
     2	import type { Randomness } from '@platform/runtime';
     3	import { createCorrelationId } from './createCorrelationId';
     4	import type { ObservabilityFacade } from './observabilityFacade';
     5	import { redact } from './redact';
     6	import { createConsoleSink } from './sinks/createConsoleSink';
     7	import { createNoOpSink } from './sinks/createNoOpSink';
     8	import { createRingBufferSink } from './sinks/createRingBufferSink';
     9	import type { TelemetryRecord } from './telemetryRecord';
    10
    11	const FALLBACK_CORRELATION_ID = '0'.repeat(32);
    12
    13	const LOG_LEVEL_SEVERITY = {
    14	  debug: 0,
    15	  info: 1,
    16	  warn: 2,
    17	  error: 3,
    18	  silent: 4,
    19	} as const;
    20
    21	export type ObservabilityDependencies = {
    22	  configuration: Pick<Configuration, 'observabilitySink' | 'logLevel'>;
    23	  randomness: Randomness;
    24	};
    25
    26	export type BufferHandle = { read: () => readonly TelemetryRecord[] } | null;
    27
    28	export type Observability = {
    29	  facade: ObservabilityFacade;
    30	  bufferHandle: BufferHandle;
    31	};
    32
    33	export function createObservability(
    34	  dependencies: ObservabilityDependencies,
    35	): Observability {
    36	  const { sink, bufferHandle } = createSink(
    37	    dependencies.configuration.observabilitySink,
    38	  );
    39	  const thresholdSeverity =
    40	    LOG_LEVEL_SEVERITY[dependencies.configuration.logLevel];
    41
    42	  function dispatch(record: TelemetryRecord): void {
    43	    try {
    44	      if (
    45	        record.kind === 'log' &&
    46	        LOG_LEVEL_SEVERITY[record.level] < thresholdSeverity
    47	      ) {
    48	        return;
    49	      }
    50	      sink(redact(record));
    51	    } catch {
    52	      // invariant 59: an observability call never throws into application code.
    53	    }
    54	  }
    55
    56	  const facade: ObservabilityFacade = {
    57	    logger: {
    58	      debug: (event, attributes) =>
    59	        dispatch(logRecord('debug', event, attributes)),
    60	      info: (event, attributes) =>
    61	        dispatch(logRecord('info', event, attributes)),
    62	      warn: (event, attributes) =>
    63	        dispatch(logRecord('warn', event, attributes)),
    64	      error: (event, attributes) =>
    65	        dispatch(logRecord('error', event, attributes)),
    66	    },
    67	    tracer: {
    68	      recordTiming: (record) => dispatch({ kind: 'timing', timing: record }),
    69	      startInteraction: () => {
    70	        // invariant 59 covers the whole facade, not only dispatch-routed
    71	        // calls: a throwing randomness source must not escape either.
    72	        try {
    73	          return createCorrelationId(dependencies.randomness);
    74	        } catch {
    75	          return FALLBACK_CORRELATION_ID;
    76	        }
    77	      },
    78	    },
    79	    analytics: {
    80	      track: (name, payload) => dispatch({ kind: 'analytics', name, payload }),
    81	    },
    82	  };
    83
    84	  return { facade, bufferHandle };
    85	}
    86
    87	function logRecord(
    88	  level: 'debug' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error',
    89	  event: string,
    90	  attributes: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined,
    91	): TelemetryRecord {
    92	  return {
    93	    kind: 'log',
    94	    level,
    95	    event,
    96	    ...(attributes !== undefined ? { attributes } : {}),
    97	  };
    98	}
    99
   100	function createSink(sinkKind: Configuration['observabilitySink']): {
   101	  sink: (record: TelemetryRecord) => void;
   102	  bufferHandle: BufferHandle;
   103	} {
   104	  if (sinkKind === 'buffer') {
   105	    const ringBuffer = createRingBufferSink();
   106	    return { sink: ringBuffer.write, bufferHandle: { read: ringBuffer.read } };
   107	  }
   108	  if (sinkKind === 'console') {
   109	    return { sink: createConsoleSink(), bufferHandle: null };
   110	  }
   111	  return { sink: createNoOpSink(), bufferHandle: null };
   112	}

     1	import type { TelemetryRecord } from '../telemetryRecord';
     2
     3	export function createConsoleSink(): (record: TelemetryRecord) => void {
     4	  return (record) => {
     5	    if (record.kind === 'log') {
     6	      console[record.level](record.event, record.attributes);
     7	      return;
     8	    }
     9	    console.debug(record.kind, record);
    10	  };
    11	}
     1	import type { TelemetryRecord } from '../telemetryRecord';
     2
     3	const RING_BUFFER_CAPACITY = 256;
     4
     5	export type RingBufferSink = {
     6	  write: (record: TelemetryRecord) => void;
     7	  read: () => readonly TelemetryRecord[];
     8	};
     9
    10	export function createRingBufferSink(): RingBufferSink {
    11	  const buffer: TelemetryRecord[] = [];
    12	  let writeCursor = 0;
    13	  let wrapped = false;
    14
    15	  function write(record: TelemetryRecord): void {
    16	    buffer[writeCursor] = record;
    17	    writeCursor += 1;
    18	    if (writeCursor >= RING_BUFFER_CAPACITY) {
    19	      writeCursor = 0;
    20	      wrapped = true;
    21	    }
    22	  }
    23
    24	  function read(): readonly TelemetryRecord[] {
    25	    if (!wrapped) return buffer.slice(0, writeCursor);
    26	    return [...buffer.slice(writeCursor), ...buffer.slice(0, writeCursor)];
    27	  }
    28
    29	  return { write, read };
    30	}

     1	export type CspMode = 'production' | 'development';
     2
     3	// frame-ancestors is deliberately never emitted here: a meta-tag CSP
     4	// ignores it and browsers warn about it (invariant 99), so it ships as
     5	// a response header instead, from public/_headers.
     6	export function buildContentSecurityPolicy(
     7	  mode: CspMode,
     8	  apiBaseUrl: string,
     9	): string {
    10	  const isDevelopment = mode === 'development';
    11
    12	  const directives = [
    13	    "default-src 'self'",
    14	    "object-src 'none'",
    15	    "base-uri 'self'",
    16	    "img-src 'self' data:",
    17	    isDevelopment ? "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'" : "style-src 'self'",
    18	    "font-src 'self'",
    19	    isDevelopment
    20	      ? "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'"
    21	      : "script-src 'self'",
    22	    isDevelopment
    23	      ? `connect-src 'self' ${apiBaseUrl} ws:`
    24	      : `connect-src 'self' ${apiBaseUrl}`,
    25	  ];
    26
    27	  return directives.join('; ');
    28	}

     1	#!/usr/bin/env node
     2	// Tripwire against secrets, not a proof of absence (invariants 20, 133).
     3	// Two halves that run at different times because they scan different
     4	// things: --source-only runs in `npm run lint` over src/, --bundle-only
     5	// runs in `npm run verify:build` over dist/ immediately after the build
     6	// and FAILS (not skips) when dist/ is missing.
     7	import { existsSync, globSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
     8
     9	const mode = process.argv.includes('--bundle-only')
    10	  ? 'bundle'
    11	  : process.argv.includes('--source-only')
    12	    ? 'source'
    13	    : null;
    14
    15	if (!mode) {
    16	  console.error('assert-no-secrets: pass --source-only or --bundle-only');
    17	  process.exit(1);
    18	}
    19
    20	const HIGH_ENTROPY_HEX_OR_BASE64 =
    21	  /\b(?:[0-9a-f]{32,}|[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2})\b/i;
    22	const SECRET_KEYWORDS = [
    23	  /apiKey/i,
    24	  /authorization/i,
    25	  /bearer\s/i,
    26	  /AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}/,
    27	];
    28
    29	function findKeywordSecrets(source, filePath, violations) {
    30	  for (const pattern of SECRET_KEYWORDS) {
    31	    if (pattern.test(source)) {
    32	      violations.push(`${filePath}: matches secret keyword pattern ${pattern}`);
    33	    }
    34	  }
    35	  const entropyMatch = source.match(HIGH_ENTROPY_HEX_OR_BASE64);
    36	  if (entropyMatch) {
    37	    violations.push(
    38	      `${filePath}: high-entropy literal found (${entropyMatch[0].slice(0, 12)}...)`,
    39	    );
    40	  }
    41	}
    42
    43	function findSuppressedRules(source, filePath, violations) {
    44	  const bannedRulePrefixes = [
    45	    'boundaries/',
    46	    'no-restricted-',
    47	    'no-explicit-any',
    48	    'no-non-null-assertion',
    49	  ];
    50	  const disableLines = source
    51	    .split('\n')
    52	    .filter((line) => /eslint-disable/.test(line));
    53
    54	  for (const line of disableLines) {
    55	    for (const prefix of bannedRulePrefixes) {
    56	      if (line.includes(prefix)) {
    57	        violations.push(
    58	          `${filePath}: eslint-disable suppresses "${prefix}" - suppression is not permitted for this rule`,
    59	        );
    60	      }
    61	    }
    62	  }
    63	}
    64
    65	function checkTrackedEnvFiles(violations) {
    66	  const envFiles = readdirSync('.').filter(
    67	    (name) => name.startsWith('.env') && name !== '.env.example',
    68	  );
    69	  for (const envFile of envFiles) {
    70	    violations.push(
    71	      `${envFile}: a .env file other than .env.example must never be tracked`,
    72	    );
    73	  }
    74	}
    75
    76	const explicitTargets = process.argv
    77	  .slice(2)
    78	  .filter((arg) => !arg.startsWith('--'));
    79	const violations = [];
    80
    81	if (mode === 'source') {
    82	  if (explicitTargets.length === 0) checkTrackedEnvFiles(violations);
    83	  for (const filePath of explicitTargets.length > 0
    84	    ? explicitTargets
    85	    : globSync('src/**/*.{ts,tsx}')) {
    86	    const source = readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8');
    87	    findKeywordSecrets(source, filePath, violations);
    88	    findSuppressedRules(source, filePath, violations);
    89	  }
    90	} else {
    91	  if (explicitTargets.length === 0 && !existsSync('dist')) {
    92	    console.error(
    93	      'assert-no-secrets --bundle-only: dist/ is missing - run npm run build first',
    94	    );
    95	    process.exit(1);
    96	  }
    97	  for (const filePath of explicitTargets.length > 0
    98	    ? explicitTargets
    99	    : globSync('dist/**/*.{js,html,css}')) {
   100	    const source = readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8');
   101	    findKeywordSecrets(source, filePath, violations);
   102	  }
   103	}
   104
   105	if (violations.length > 0) {
   106	  console.error(`assert-no-secrets --${mode}-only: secrets found:`);
   107	  for (const violation of violations) {
   108	    console.error(`  - ${violation}`);
   109	  }
   110	  process.exit(1);
   111	}
   112
   113	process.exit(0);
     1	import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
     2	import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
     3	import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
     4	import { join } from 'node:path';
     5	import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
     6
     7	function runScript(
     8	  scriptPath: string,
     9	  args: string[] = [],
    10	  options: { cwd?: string } = {},
    11	): { status: number; output: string } {
    12	  try {
    13	    const output = execFileSync('node', [scriptPath, ...args], {
    14	      encoding: 'utf-8',
    15	      cwd: options.cwd,
    16	    });
    17	    return { status: 0, output };
    18	  } catch (error) {
    19	    const execError = error as {
    20	      status?: number;
    21	      stdout?: string;
    22	      stderr?: string;
    23	    };
    24	    return {
    25	      status: execError.status ?? 1,
    26	      output: `${execError.stdout ?? ''}${execError.stderr ?? ''}`,
    27	    };
    28	  }
    29	}

    31	describe('assert-domain-vocabulary', () => {
    32	  it('the vocabulary script matches whole identifier segments and not substrings', () => {
    33	    const probeDir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'domain-vocabulary-'));
    34	    const safeFile = join(probeDir, 'safe.tmp.ts');
    35	    const bannedFile = join(probeDir, 'banned.tmp.ts');
    36
    37	    // "encodeURIComponent" segments as encode/URI/Component - none of

    40	      safeFile,

    42	    );

    45
    46	    const scriptPath = 'scripts/assert-domain-vocabulary.mjs';

   143	99. The delivered HTML carries a Content-Security-Policy meta tag that at minimum sets `default-src 'self'`, `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'self'`, and a `connect-src` that includes the configured API base URL. It does NOT set `frame-ancestors`: that directive is ignored inside a meta tag and browsers warn about it, so including it would buy nothing and force a console allow-list entry that invariant 100 depends on staying empty. Clickjacking protection is a response header instead - see invariant 99a. `img-src` allows only `'self'` and `data:` - no remote host. Phase 3 reads the live `users` payload, learns the actual avatar hosts, and widens `img-src` as a reviewed change with a decision-log entry.    144	99a. Framing protection ships as a response header, because the meta tag cannot carry it. The build output contains a `_headers` file declaring `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'` for every path, which Cloudflare Pages serves as a real header. It is deliberately the only directive in the header: the meta tag stays the single place the rest of the policy is read, and two half-policies that can disagree is the failure mode this split avoids. That exclusivity is **asserted, not just described**: the build-output check compares `dist/_headers` against its exact expected content byte for byte - the `/*` path line and the one indented header line and nothing else - so an added directive fails the check exactly as a missing one does. An exact-content assertion is what the sibling `_redirects` check already uses (invariant 124), and it is required here for a second reason: Cloudflare's `_headers` format silently ignores a header line that is not indented under its path block, so a containment check would pass a file that ships no framing protection at all. The deployed smoke run then asserts the header actually arrives on the live response, which is the only check that can distinguish a correct file from a correctly-formatted file the host did not apply. The residual gap the previous hosting choice left - no framing protection at all - is closed rather than recorded.
   145	100. No route produces a CSP violation, and the console carries no error or warning, in both the development server and the production build. The allow-list is empty for every spec but one. The forced-error spec aborts a lazy route chunk, and an aborted subresource makes the BROWSER log a network error that no application code can intercept; that spec therefore asserts an exact expected set - the single aborted-request entry, matched by URL - and fails on any other entry. An exact expected set is not an open-ended allow-list: it fails on a new entry exactly as an empty assertion would, which is the property this invariant depends on. Widening it, or adding an entry to any other spec, requires the same argument as downgrading a lint rule.

   148	### The quality pipeline
   149
   150	102. Each **gating check** is one npm script, and CI runs exactly those scripts. There is no gate that exists only in the workflow file, so a check that passes locally passes in CI for the same reason. Infrastructure setup steps are exempt and named explicitly - `npm ci` and `npx playwright install` are the whole allow-list; a run line that is neither an npm script nor an allow-listed setup command fails the workflow-parse test. The rule's scope is the **`verify` job**, which is where every gate lives. The `deploy` job is not a gate - it runs only after `verify` has passed, only on `main`, and it cannot make a failing change green - so its steps are outside this rule. That is not a loophole for smuggling a check into the workflow: the deploy job's one assertion (invariant 123's deployment-URL comparison) is about the deployment itself, which by definition has no local equivalent to run, and it is the only such step this phase permits. A new `run:` line in the `deploy` job that checks the *code* rather than the deployment is a violation of this invariant's intent and is caught in review.
   151	103. One GitHub Actions workflow runs on pull requests and on pushes to `main`, in this order: typecheck, lint, format check, unit tests with coverage, build, build-output assertions, size budgets, e2e. The build-output step exists because several checks can only inspect `dist` - the bundle secrets scan, the base-path scan, the route and catalogue chunk assertions, the kit-route absence check and the `_redirects`/`_headers` files - and a check that runs before the build exists is not a check.
   152	104. Typecheck failing means the code is not type-sound. `strict` is enabled in `tsconfig.app.json` (it is currently missing), and type-aware ESLint rules are configured so lint sees types.
   153	105. `any` and non-null assertions fail lint. A suppression comment for a type or boundary rule requires an adjacent justification, and none appears in shipped `src` for those rules.
   154	106. Lint failing means either a correctness rule or an architecture rule was broken: boundaries, restricted imports, `jsx-a11y`, `react-hooks`, `i18next` literals, testing-library and Playwright hygiene. Lint output names the rule so the category is unambiguous.
   155	107. Format check failing means Prettier would rewrite a file, including Tailwind class order. Formatting is never argued in review.

   159	111. Build failing means the production bundle cannot be produced. The build runs the typecheck as part of `npm run build`.
   160	112. Size budgets are checked by `size-limit` against the production build, and every emitted chunk class has an entry: the initial payload (entry plus vendor) at most 150 kB gzipped, the stylesheet at most 15 kB gzipped, each per-route chunk at most 30 kB gzipped, and each lazily loaded catalogue chunk at most 5 kB gzipped. Exceeding a budget fails CI with actual and limit printed. The figure was originally set at 100 kB against an estimate of 85-90 kB for the **fixed runtime dependency set alone** (react-dom, react-router, zod, i18next, react-i18next, web-vitals). Wiring the real router in M5 measured the entry at 112.77 kB and busted that number; an isolated tree-shaken probe of `createBrowserRouter`/`RouterProvider` alone put react-router's own weight at roughly 31 kB gzipped, showing the original estimate had undercounted react-router specifically rather than the build regressing. Per this invariant's own rule, the number was revisited with the user rather than silently raised, and the user set the corrected budget at 150 kB. That is measured from the first milestone rather than the last, and if a future measurement contradicts the estimate again the number is again revisited with the user, never silently raised.
   161	113. E2E runs Playwright against the production build with `route()` mocks.    162	114. The Playwright HTML report is uploaded as a CI artifact on both success and failure, so a failing run is diagnosable from the run page without reproducing locally.

   164	116. A live smoke job against the real database exists as a manually triggered job only. It never runs on a pull request or on `main`, and its failure cannot block a merge. Its test file lives **outside `src`** and outside every default Vitest project, so no gating command can collect it even by accident; it runs only under its own config.

The printed field names are the deliverable - `docs/reference.md` records the user record's field names as unconfirmed and requires reading them from the live database before any schema is written, which phase 3 needs.
   166	116b. The live smoke asserts nothing about field names it printed. Discovering that the live shape changed is a phase 3 concern; phase 1 only proves the endpoint is reachable and the two expected top-level keys exist.
   167	117. CI runs on the Node version pinned in the repository, matching local development, so a version drift is a visible change rather than a mysterious failure.

   169	119. The phase is not claimed done on an unrun suite. Every claim in the phase's proof points to a run that happened.

   172
   173	120. A push to `main` deploys the built site to Cloudflare Pages from the same GitHub Actions workflow, and only after every gating check has passed. The deploy step is `wrangler pages deploy` against the already-built `dist`, so the artifact that was verified is the artifact that ships - nothing is rebuilt for the deploy.
