   176	123. The deployed site renders the placeholder home route at its root URL. The URL is the Cloudflare Pages project's production hostname, recorded **once, in one machine-readable place** - `deployment.json` at the repository root, holding the project name and the production hostname - so that the workflow, the deployed Playwright project and the documentation all read the same value rather than each carrying a copy that can drift. A prose document cannot be that place: a workflow step cannot read a sentence out of `VERIFICATION.md`, so recording it only there guarantees a second hardcoded copy in `ci.yml`. `VERIFICATION.md` and `.env.example` cite the value, and a unit test asserts the value they cite matches `deployment.json`, which is what keeps the documentation honest without making it the source. The deploy step additionally asserts that the deployment URL Wrangler reports back **is** that recorded production hostname, not a `<hash>.<project>.pages.dev` preview URL. Without that assertion a mis-configured project (invariant 126) produces a green deploy job that shipped to a preview nobody looks at, which is the one deployment failure the pipeline cannot otherwise see.
   177	124. `<deployed-base>/login` renders the placeholder login route on a direct load and after a browser refresh, not a 404. Deep links work because the build output carries a `_redirects` rule serving `index.html` with a 200 status for any unmatched path. This is the phase's third exit criterion and is proven against the deployed URL in this loop.
   178	125. Concurrent pushes to `main` do not race: a newer deploy supersedes an in-flight one rather than interleaving with it.
   179	126. The deployment depends on manual, one-time setup performed by the repository owner, and the list is exhaustive because every item on it is invisible to CI: a Cloudflare Pages project created with direct-upload (not Git integration, which would deploy without waiting for the gates); **the project's production branch set to `main`**; and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` stored as repository secrets. The token carries the Pages edit permission and nothing else. The production-branch item is load-bearing rather than administrative: Cloudflare decides production-versus-preview by comparing the upload's `--branch` against the project's configured production branch, so if they disagree, `wrangler pages deploy --branch=main` succeeds, reports a preview URL, and leaves the production hostname stale while the job stays green. Invariant 123's URL assertion is what turns that silent case into a failure. This whole list is named as a prerequisite in the change, so a failed first deploy is diagnosable in seconds, and no secret value appears in the repository (invariant 133).
   180
   181	126a. Invariants 123 and 124 cannot be proven before merge, and the phase does not pretend otherwise. Invariant 121 forbids preview deployments, so no pull-request run produces a URL to test; this is a deliberate trade - preview deploys would make the exit criterion provable on the pull request, and they are rejected because they put a deploy surface and a live token on every pull request, including forks. The consequence is an explicit obligation rather than a gap: after the merge to `main`, the deploy job runs and `npm run e2e:deployed` is run against the recorded production hostname, its output is captured as evidence, and **the phase is not complete until it passes** (invariant 119). If it fails, the phase is not silently done - the failure is the loop's, a fix lands on a follow-up branch through the same gates, and the deployed run is repeated. No milestone boundary and no pull-request run may claim invariants 123 or 124 as verified.
   182
   183	### What must not be true at the end of this phase
   184
   185	127. No login behavior exists: no credential-to-secret derivation, no lookup table, no `/secrets` request, no password handling of any kind.
   186	128. No session exists: there is no logged-in user concept, no route guard and no logout. Nothing in the app writes to `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB or a service worker cache, and a use of any of those globals in `src` fails lint - the rule that carries the storage half of this invariant, inherited from the withdrawn caching set. The banned set is enumerated, not illustrative: `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `indexedDB`, `caches` (the `CacheStorage` global, which is the service-worker cache this invariant names) and `navigator.serviceWorker`. Each is banned in **both** the bare-identifier and the member forms - `window.localStorage`, `globalThis.sessionStorage` and their siblings - because a bare-identifier rule alone matches neither, which is the same pairing the network ban of invariant 21 already uses. A storage global reached by computed member access is not lint-detectable; that residue is review-carried and named as such. Phase 2 removes the `sessionStorage` entry from that rule with a decision-log line, because the session record is what first needs it.
   187	129. No hierarchy behavior exists: no `buildForest`, no `flattenVisible`, no tree widget, no users request, no user schema, no avatar data.
   188	130. No repository module for a real resource exists. The HTTP client is exercised by tests against a fake transport and fixtures, not against a domain resource.
   189	131. No Vite template cruft remains in `src` or `public`: the template's `App` component, its stylesheet and its unused logo assets are gone. (The README rewrite belongs to phase 3 per ROADMAP.md and is out of scope here.)
   190	132. No placeholder page contains lorem ipsum, a fake form, or a control that does nothing when activated.
   191	133. No secret, token, API key, credential or private endpoint appears in the repository, in the bundle, or in any environment file. Everything shipped is public by construction, because a static client bundle is public.
   192	134. No runtime dependency is added beyond what these invariants require, and each added dependency is justified against the size budget. The allow-list is exactly `react`, `react-dom`, `react-router`, `zod`, `i18next`, `react-i18next` and `web-vitals`; a check fails when `dependencies` stops matching it, so a new one is a deliberate edit rather than a drift. Specifically excluded: no data-fetching library, no component library, no telemetry vendor SDK, no polyfill for something the pinned Node and target browsers already have. `web-vitals` is on the list by the explicit decision recorded at invariant 52, not by default.
   193	135. No check in the pipeline is disabled, skipped or set to continue-on-error to make the phase green.
   194	136. No feature-shaped code is parked in `app`, `shared` or `platform` in anticipation of phases 2 and 3. An abstraction with no caller in this phase is not built.
   195
   196	## Goals / Non-goals
   197
   198	**Goals**
   199
   200	- The four layers exist and their import rules are enforced by lint, with both forbidden edges demonstrated failing and then reverted.
   201	- The platform layer adapts the outside world: typed validated configuration, one HTTP client with timeout, bounded retry, trace propagation and a typed error union, an observability facade with swappable sinks and a redaction layer, and i18n with lazy per-feature namespaces.
   202	- A domain-free UI kit carries the mockups' visual language in light and dark, at WCAG AA, with visible focus, reduced-motion support and logical properties, and all eight components are proven in a real browser through a development-only kit route that never reaches production.
   203	- The router, provider stack and root error boundary compose an app that renders `/login`, `/` and a not-found route.
   204	- The whole quality pipeline runs in CI in a defined order, with coverage thresholds, size budgets and an e2e report artifact.
   205	- `main` deploys itself to Cloudflare Pages after the gates pass, and the deployed URL renders the placeholder login route on a direct load.
   206
   207	**Non-goals**
   208
   209	Belonging to phase 2:
   210
   211	- Login form, credential-to-secret derivation, the `/secrets` lookup, authentication error states, session persistence, the route guard and the `from` redirect.
   212
   213	Belonging to phase 3:
   214
   215	- The tree domain, tolerant per-row validation, the users request, the ARIA tree widget and its keyboard contract, URL-persisted expansion state, the header with the signed-in user and logout, the summary line and per-row report counts, and the README rewrite.
   216
   217	Deliberately not built at all (ARCHITECTURE.md section 7):
   218
   219	- Response caching - in-flight dedupe, TTL, stale-while-revalidate. Withdrawn from the roadmap on 2026-08-13, not deferred to a later phase: no phase builds `platform/cache`, and the repository per resource is the seam a cache attaches behind if one is ever wanted. Invariants 36-44 are retired with it.
   220	- Virtualized rendering. Unnecessary at 33 rows; `flattenVisible` will emit the row model a windowing layer consumes.
   221	- Real authentication. Impossible against this API from a static client; `features/auth` isolates the lookup so a BFF-issued cookie replaces one module.
   222	- Offline support and service workers. A 9KB public payload does not justify a cache lifecycle; the repository layer is where a persistent cache would attach.
   223	- Search, filtering and org editing. Outside GOAL.md.
   224	- A second locale, SSR and a component library. The infrastructure supports each; none is needed.
   225	- Vendor telemetry. The facade defines the contract; a real sink is a sink swap.
   226
   227	Also out of scope for this phase specifically:
   228
   229	- A theme switcher, a design-system documentation site, or a component gallery that ships. The development-only kit route of invariant 86a is in scope and is not a gallery: it is a verification surface that renders the state inventory, carries no documentation and no navigation, and is absent from the production build by invariant 86b. A gallery page reachable by a user of the deployed site remains out of scope.
   230	- Performance tuning beyond meeting the stated size budgets.
   231	- Any CI job that gates on the live third-party database.
   232
   233	## Open questions
   234
   235	All four questions raised during drafting were settled with the user on 2026-08-13, before TECH.md was written. None remain open.
   236
   237	- **Placeholder fidelity** - resolved: the `/login` placeholder stays generic; mockup screen `1a` lands whole in phase 2. Encoded as invariant 96a.
   238	- **Dark theme values** - resolved: derive the dark palette over the same token names and let the automated WCAG AA contrast assertion be the gate. No separate human review round before phase 2; invariants 71 and 72 already carry the constraints, and the design flag is off for this loop because the mockups are the existing visual reference.
   239	- **CSP image sources** - resolved: ship the tight policy now (`img-src 'self' data:`) and widen it in phase 3 against evidence from the live payload. Encoded as invariant 99.
   240	- **Phase 1 live smoke content** - resolved: it ships as a reachability and shape probe that also prints the observed `users` field names, which phase 3 needs. Encoded as invariants 116a and 116b.
   241
   242	The G1 validation round (two independent reviewers, 42 findings, recorded under `evidence/reviews/`) raised eight further questions. All were settled on 2026-08-13 and encoded here rather than left open:
   243
   244	- **Is the request deadline per attempt or per logical request?** Per logical request - invariant 23.
   245	- **What outcome does a caller-initiated abort produce?** Its own `cancelled` outcome, leaving the four-member failure union untouched - invariants 25 and 33.
   246	- **What does a read see during a revalidation, and what does a failed revalidation do to freshness?** Moot: caching is withdrawn (invariants 36-44). The cost of answering this question, and the two either side of it, is what the withdrawal decision was made on.
   247	- **What happens to an in-flight load when `invalidate` or `clear` runs?** Moot, as above.
   248	- **What does a missing key render in production?** The same visible marker as everywhere else, reported through the facade - invariant 63.
   249	- **How are the five kit components with no product surface proven?** The development-only kit route - invariants 86a and 86b.
   250	- **Does the empty console allow-list cover the forced-error spec?** Yes; React's `onCaughtError` routes the error to observability instead of the console - invariant 100.
   251	- **Does a failed navigation emit `app.route_viewed`?** No - invariant 47a.
   252
   253	One question the reviewers raised is deliberately **not** settled here, because phase 1 cannot answer it: whether the `traceparent` header triggers a CORS preflight against the live database. The live smoke runs under Node, where CORS is not enforced, so the probe cannot discover it. It is recorded as a phase 2 risk in TECH.md rather than as a phase 1 invariant.
   940
   941	Worktree fan-out: there is no independent pair left. M3 and M4 were the only candidates, and M4 depends on M3 for the configuration flag that mounts the kit route, so the phase runs sequentially - which was the recommendation regardless. M3 and M4 both edit `package.json` (dependency additions), `vitest.config.ts` (coverage `exclude` entries) and `eslint.config.js` (rule overrides for test files), which is a guaranteed three-way merge on files where a bad merge is silent - a dropped ESLint override does not fail a build, it removes a check. The wall-clock saving is one milestone's worth of work on a six-milestone phase; the risk is losing an enforcement rule without noticing. If fan-out is used regardless, the precondition is that every shared configuration edit either lands in M2 or is confined to a per-milestone file that M5 merges deliberately.
   942
   943	## Testing and validation
   944
   945	Every invariant is accounted for. Categories: **unit** (Vitest), **e2e** (Playwright), **lint** (a rule that must be demonstrated failing), **script** (a repository assertion script or config-parsing test), **CI** (a job outcome), **deployed** (proven against the live URL), **review** (human judgement, flagged where it is the only mechanism).

   947	### Layer boundaries (1-12)
   948
   949	- 1 - lint: `boundaries/no-unknown-files` and `boundaries/no-unknown`. Demonstrated by adding `src/stray.ts` and capturing the error, then reverting (folded into the M2 evidence run).
   950	- 2, 3, 4, 5 - lint: the four `boundaries/element-types` rows. 5 is additionally demonstrated by adding an `@shared` import to a platform module during the M2 evidence run.

   952	- 7 - lint + evidence: `specs/phase-1-setup/evidence/boundaries-deep-import.txt` (invariant 11).

Signatures carrying a domain type cannot be checked mechanically while no domain type exists - review carries that half in phase 1 and the lint boundary carries it from phase 3.
   954	- 9 - unit: a test asserting `src/features/auth/index.ts` and `src/features/hierarchy/index.ts` exist and export the documented names.
   955	- 10, 11 - evidence files above, captured and reverted in M2.

   959
   960	- 13 - lint (`no-restricted-syntax`), demonstrated by adding a second `import.meta.env` read during the M2 evidence run and capturing the error.
   961	- 14 - unit: a `@ts-expect-error` assignment test plus a runtime test asserting the frozen object rejects a write.
   962	- 15 - unit: schema tests per key, valid and invalid.
   963	- 16 - unit: `main.tsx`'s startup path extracted into a testable `bootstrap(root, environment)` function; a test with an invalid environment asserts the error screen renders, the router does not, and a report was emitted.

   969	### HTTP client (21-35)
   970
   971	- 21 - lint + unit. The lint half is `no-restricted-globals` for `fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest`, `no-restricted-properties` for `globalThis.fetch` and `window.fetch`, and `no-restricted-syntax` for `new WebSocket` and `navigator.sendBeacon`, all scoped to `src` outside `createFetchTransport.ts`, demonstrated failing in the M2 evidence run. A lint rule cannot catch an aliased indirection (`const f = globalThis['fet' + 'ch']`), so the unit half backs it: `vitest.setup.ts` replaces `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket` and `sendBeacon` with throwing stubs in BOTH projects, so any transport reached by any route fails the suite that touches it. Neither half alone discriminates; together they cover the static and the dynamic case.
   972	- 22 - unit: a `@ts-expect-error` test for an absolute URL, plus a runtime test for a protocol-relative path.
   973	- 23 - unit: the deadline is per LOGICAL request. The test arms a client with an 8000 ms deadline against a transport whose first attempt fails at 3000 ms and whose retry never responds, advances the fake clock to 8000 ms, and asserts the call settles as `{ kind: 'timeout' }` at 8000 ms rather than at 8000 ms after the retry began. A per-attempt implementation fails this test, which is the point - the previous "advance past the deadline" phrasing passed under either design.
   974	- 24, 25 - unit: `AbortSignal.any` composition; a caller abort asserted to produce the `cancelled` outcome, not a failure, and asserted not to retry and not to emit an error record. A test also asserts a pre-aborted signal returns `cancelled` without any transport call.
   975	- 26, 27, 28, 29 - unit: one table-driven test per rule (attempt count, method, failure class, exact delay from the fake randomness).
   976	- 30 - unit: the `traceparent` header is asserted against a regex and against the tracker's `currentCorrelationId()`.
   977	- 31 - unit: a spy sink receives one timing record per attempt with the documented fields and a shared `requestId`.
   978	- 32 - unit: the whole http suite runs with the fake transport and the network stub in `vitest.setup.ts` active. This is only true because the `platform` Vitest project now loads that setup file (section 6.1); it previously did not, which made this entry's claim false about its own configuration.
   979	- 33 - unit: an exhaustive `switch` over `HttpFailure` with no default branch, which fails `tsc` if a member is added - the typecheck is the assertion. A second `@ts-expect-error` test asserts that a `cancelled` outcome does NOT typecheck as a member of `HttpFailure`, which is what keeps cancellation off the error path.
   980	- 34, 35 - unit: a transport throwing a `TypeError` yields `{ kind: 'network' }`; a 500 with a body containing a token yields a failure object asserted to contain none of the body's characters.
   981
   982	### Caching (36-44) - withdrawn
   983
   984	No checks, because no behavior: invariants 36-44 are retired with the cache (section 3.3). The one rule that survives them, the storage-global ban, is checked under invariant 128.

   986	### Observability (45-59)
   987
   988	- 45a - lint: the `no-restricted-syntax` selector on `globalThis.__hierarchyTreeTelemetry`, overridden for `createRuntime.ts` alone, so any other module touching the handle fails lint.
   989	- 45 - lint (`no-restricted-imports` on the sinks path) + unit: `Object.keys(facade)` is exactly `['logger','tracer','analytics']`. The assertion is on the FACADE, which is what features and the app hold; `create-observability` additionally returns `bufferHandle`, and a separate test asserts the handle is null unless the buffer sink is selected.
   990	- 46 - unit: three configurations, three sink types, asserted by behavior.
   991	- 47 - unit + e2e: unit drives `tracer.recordTiming` through the http client's fake transport and asserts the same id on the request record, the boundary report and the analytics event. E2E asserts the two-way equality a fetch-free app can actually exhibit - the `route_viewed` event and any boundary report inside one navigation share an id - and section 3.4 records that the third leg is first exercised by a real request in phase 2 rather than pretending it is proven here.
   992	- 47a - unit + e2e: one interaction owns one correlation id for its whole lifecycle. Unit drives `interaction-tracker` through a fake router subscription and asserts a new id per navigation, the initial load included; e2e asserts exactly one `app.route_viewed` per successful navigation and NONE on the aborted-chunk navigation, which is the half that distinguishes the tracker from one that emits on navigation start.
   993	- 48 - unit: 300 writes into a 256-capacity buffer; length stays 256, the oldest is gone, and `read()` returns them oldest-first across the wrap, so the handle's ordering contract holds after the cursor has wrapped rather than only before.
   994	- 49 - e2e: `telemetry-buffer.spec.ts` reads the handle.
   995	- 50, 51 - unit: `@ts-expect-error` tests for an unknown name and a malformed payload; the typecheck is the assertion.
   996	- 52 - unit: the `web-vitals` module is faked with `vi.mock('web-vitals', ...)`, whose `onLCP`, `onINP` and `onCLS` capture the callback they are handed instead of observing anything. The test registers the reporter, invokes each captured callback with a metric object, and asserts three `app.web_vital` events carrying `LCP`, `INP` and `CLS` with the passed values. A second assertion checks each of the three registration functions was called exactly once.
   997	- 53 - unit: two cases against the same mock - `PerformanceObserver` deleted from `globalThis`, and the mocked `onLCP`/`onINP`/`onCLS` made to throw on registration. Both assert the reporter returns normally, emits no analytics event, and produces no `console` call (a spy on every console method asserts zero calls).
   998	- 54 - unit: a sink spy asserting `dispatch` redacted before the sink saw the record, for all three interfaces.
   999	- 55, 56 - unit: invariant 55 says "at any depth", so the test exercises depth rather than one instance of each key - `password` at depths 1, 3 and 6, `TOKEN` inside an array inside an array, `apiSecret` as a URL search parameter, and a key differing only in case (`Secret`, `TOKEN`). It asserts no sink received any original value and every key survived. Two structural cases are included because redaction walks caller data: a cyclic object (asserting termination and no throw) and an object appearing twice by shared reference (asserting both occurrences are redacted, not just the first).
  1000	- 57 - unit: level `warn` configured, `logger.debug` called, zero sink calls.
  1001	- 58 - lint (21) + e2e. The route handler allows same-origin traffic so the app can load its own chunks, which means a sink posting telemetry back to the app's own origin would pass; the discriminating half is therefore a unit test asserting each of the three sink modules' import graph contains no transport module and no network global, plus the sendBeacon stub from invariant 21's setup. Named honestly: the e2e half constrains cross-origin, the unit half constrains same-origin.
  1002	- 59 - unit, two cases: a sink that always throws, AND a payload whose property getter throws, which exercises the redaction traversal rather than the sink. The second is the one that discriminates - it fails against the earlier design where the `try/catch` wrapped only the sink call. Both assert the caller returns normally and a component render completes.

  1005
  1006	- 60 - lint (`i18next/no-literal-string`), demonstrated failing on an added JSX literal in the M2 evidence run.
  1007	- 61 - unit: the catalogue files exist at the documented paths and the i18next instance reports the expected namespaces.
  1008	- 62 - unit + build output: a test asserts each feature's `loadTranslations` registers only its own namespace and is idempotent under concurrent calls. The build-output half reads Vite's manifest and asserts on the CHUNK GRAPH, per section 3.5: the login route chunk's transitive imports include the `auth` catalogue chunk and exclude the `hierarchy` one, and vice versa. It does NOT grep the login chunk for a hierarchy key - section 3.5 establishes that a dynamically imported catalogue is its own chunk, so that grep passes against a correct and a broken build alike.

  1012	- 66 - unit + e2e: `document.documentElement.lang === 'en'` and `dir === 'ltr'` after render, plus a direct unit test of `localeDirection` over a table (`en` -> `ltr`, `ar`/`he`/`fa`/`ur` -> `rtl`, unknown -> `ltr`).
  1013	- 67 - script: `scripts/assert-no-physical-properties.mjs`, run inside `npm run lint`.
  1014	- 68 - e2e: the direction override is installed with `page.addInitScript` BEFORE navigation, so it survives the application's own startup write to `dir`. The earlier procedure set `dir="rtl"` and then reloaded, which let startup reset it to `ltr` and left the test inspecting the wrong direction while passing. With the override in place: load both routes and the kit route, assert no horizontal overflow (`scrollWidth <= clientWidth`), and assert a mirrored inline-start indicator - an element whose computed `padding-inline-start` resolves on the right-hand side - which is what actually discriminates logical properties from physical ones. A screenshot goes into the report artifact.

  1016	### UI kit (69-87)
  1017
  1018	- 69 - unit: `src/shared/ui/index.ts` exports exactly the eight components.
  1019	- 70, 71 - unit: the token parser test asserts every color token declared in `@theme` also appears in the dark block; a grep asserts no raw color literal in `src/shared/ui` or `src/app`.
  1020	- 72 - unit: the contrast test of section 4.2.
  1021	- 73 - unit: the dark block is inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`; a grep asserts no theme-switcher code exists.
  1022	- 74 - unit: a `:focus-visible` rule exists and no `outline: none` appears without a replacement; the contrast test covers the focus-ring pairs; e2e tabs through each route and asserts a focused element has a non-zero outline width via `getComputedStyle`.
  1023	- 75 - unit: with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` stubbed, `getComputedStyle` on the skeleton reports zero animation duration (jsdom's computed-style support is thin, so this assertion is written against the emitted CSS rule text if the stub proves unreliable - stated as the fallback rather than discovered later).
  1024	- 76 - unit + e2e. Unit: `Skeleton` requires width and height props (`@ts-expect-error` when omitted) and renders them as static utility classes, with an explicit assertion that it emits NO `style` attribute (which the production CSP would block - section 4.3). The unit half proves the props are required, not that layout is stable, so the discriminating half is e2e on the kit route: measure an element's box, swap the skeleton for content of the same named size, and assert the bounding box is unchanged. Prop presence alone never proved zero layout shift, and the earlier entry claimed it did.
  1025	- 77, 78, 79 - unit: attribute assertions; the initials fallback on missing source and on an `error` event; both accessible-name modes.
  1026	- 80 - unit: variants, disabled, busy (`aria-busy`, name preserved, a second click ignored), asserted with `user-event`. Plus the case the earlier entry missed: a busy `type="submit"` inside a `<form>` with an `onSubmit` spy, activated by click and by Enter, asserting the form never submits. Ignoring `onClick` alone passes the first assertion and fails the second, because the native default action does not route through `onClick`.
  1027	- 81 - unit: label association via `getByLabelText`, `aria-describedby` covering hint and error, `aria-invalid`, required communication, and an assertion that no placeholder equals the label.
  1028	- 82, 83 - unit: rendered content and a focusable action button with an accessible name.
  1029	- 84 - review + the domain-vocabulary grep of invariant 8.
  1030	- 85 - lint: `i18next/no-literal-string` applies to `src/shared/ui`, and a unit test asserts each component renders nothing when given empty strings.
  1031	- 86, 86a - e2e: the two placeholder routes, the not-found route AND the development-only kit route (section 4.4) at a 320x640 viewport, asserting `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= clientWidth`. The kit route is what makes the invariant's word "every" true - `Input`, `Field`, `Avatar`, `Skeleton` and `EmptyState` appear on no product surface this phase, so without it five of the eight components were covered by nothing. jsdom cannot decide overflow, so this is deliberately not a unit test.
  1032	- 87 - unit + e2e: unit renders every component in every documented state and asserts zero axe violations once, in jsdom. The light/dark half is e2e on the kit route, run twice under Playwright's `colorScheme`, because jsdom applies no stylesheet and axe's colour-contrast rule does not run there - a jsdom "dark" pass asserts on a byte-identical DOM. The documented-state inventory lives in the kit route itself, so a component state that exists but is not listed is visible as a gap in one file rather than spread across test files.
  1033	- 86b - script: part of `verify:build`. It asserts no `dist` file contains the kit route path, the kit chunk, or any state-inventory marker, so the development-only surface cannot silently become a shipped one. The check is what catches a constant-folding failure across the `environment.ts` module boundary.

  1035	### App shell (88-101)
  1036
  1037	- 88 - unit: the router is created with `basename` taken from `configuration.basePath` rather than a literal, asserted by building a router from a configuration with an overridden base path; e2e proves the real value by loading the app at `/`.
  1038	- 89 - script: the `size-limit` per-route entries fail if a route chunk is missing, plus a build-output test asserting three route chunk files exist in `dist/assets`.
  1039	- 90 - unit: `renderRoute.tsx` renders through the real stack and a test asserts each provider's context is available inside a route; a grep asserts `createBrowserRouter` appears exactly once.
  1040	- 91 - e2e + unit. E2E: the aborted lazy-chunk flow renders `ErrorState`, not a blank page, and the console recorder asserts the exact expected set of section 6.2 - the one aborted-request network entry and nothing else. It is not an empty-collection assertion, because the browser logs the aborted subresource itself and no application code can suppress that; it fails on any additional entry, including any React or React Router logging. Unit: `RootErrorBoundary` is rendered in isolation, ABOVE any router, and asserted to render `ErrorSurface` without throwing - the case that had no coverage and that the `useNavigate` design would have failed, turning the error path into the blank page the invariant forbids.
  1041	- 92 - e2e: the rendered correlation id equals the one in the buffer record, and exactly one `app.error_boundary_shown` record exists. Unit adds the primitive-throw case: `reportRootError('boom')` and `reportRootError(null)` return a correlation id and do not throw, which the `WeakSet<object>` alone would have failed.
  1042	- 93 - e2e: keyboard-only recovery - Tab to the action, Enter, assert the route re-renders. A unit test covers the root boundary's recovery separately, asserting it calls the injected `onRecover` prop rather than reaching for a router hook.
  1043	- 94 - e2e: both routes render their placeholder.
  1044	- 95 - e2e + unit: document title from the catalogue, exactly one `h1`, a `main` landmark, full keyboard reachability, axe zero violations.
  1045	- 96, 96a, 132 - review: a reviewer confirms the placeholders promise nothing, carry no nav rail, login card or brand mark, and contain no inert control or lorem ipsum. A grep for `lorem` is the only mechanical part. Flagged as review-dependent.
  1046	- 97 - unit + e2e: a grep asserts no `redirect(` and no storage access in `src`; e2e loads `/` and `/login` directly and asserts neither navigates away.
  1047	- 98 - e2e: an unmatched path renders the not-found route with a working link home, and the buffer contains no error-boundary record.
  1048	- 99 - unit: the CSP builder function is unit-tested for both modes against the required directive list - `default-src 'self'`, `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'self'`, `img-src 'self' data:` and a `connect-src` containing the configured API base URL - plus an explicit assertion that the emitted policy contains no `frame-ancestors` in either mode. E2E asserts the meta tag's content in the built page, including the absence of `frame-ancestors`.
  1049	- 100 - e2e: the console recorder on every spec, in the production preview, with an empty allow-list - including the forced-error spec, which holds because of the `createRoot` error handlers (section 5.4). The development-server half runs in the `development` Playwright project defined in section 6.2, which has its own `webServer` and port; the earlier entry named such a spec while the config defined no project for it to run in. A test asserts the recorder's allow-list is empty, so adding an entry is a visible edit.
  1050	- 99a - script + deployed: `build-output/spa-fallback.test.ts` asserts `dist/_headers` matches its expected content EXACTLY - the `/*` path line, one indented `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'` line, and nothing else - rather than merely containing that directive. The exactness is doing two jobs. It enforces 99a's "only directive" clause, which a containment check leaves entirely unasserted, so a later edit adding `script-src` or `connect-src` to `_headers` would create the two-disagreeing-policies failure mode the split exists to prevent and would pass. And it catches the format error that actually ships broken protection: Cloudflare's `_headers` syntax requires the header line to be indented under its path block and silently ignores a line that is not, so a mis-indented file passes any containment check while delivering no framing protection at all. Even exact content is still only a file check - `vite preview` sets no headers, so no local run can prove the header is served. The discriminating half is `deployed-smoke.spec.ts`, which reads the response headers of the live document and asserts the directive arrives. Both halves are named because neither alone distinguishes a correct file from a correct file the host did not apply.
  1051	- 101 - unit: `index.html` is parsed and asserted to carry `lang`, the viewport meta, a title, and a favicon link resolving to a file that is not the Vite logo.
  1052
  1053	### Quality pipeline (102-119)
  1054
  1055	- 102 - unit: the workflow-parse test (section 7.1), whose command rule applies to gating steps and exempts the named infrastructure allow-list (`npm ci`, `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`). Without that exemption the test fails against the workflow this spec itself specifies.
  1056	- 103 - unit: the same test asserts step order, now seven steps including `verify:build` after `build`.
  1057	- 104 - CI: `npm run typecheck` is a step; a unit test asserts `tsconfig.app.json` has `"strict": true` so a later removal fails the suite rather than silently weakening the build.
  1058	- 105 - lint, demonstrated failing on an added `any` and an added `!` in the M2 evidence run; plus the suppression grep in `assert-no-secrets.mjs`.
  1059	- 106 - CI: lint is its own step; the six evidence captures show the rule id in each message.
  1060	- 107 - CI: `npm run format:check` is its own step.
  1061	- 108 - CI + unit: the suite runs under jsdom with Testing Library; the network stub makes "none of them touches the network" enforced rather than claimed.
  1062	- 109 - CI: coverage thresholds in `vitest.config.ts`, failing the `test:coverage` step.
  1063	- 110 - unit: a test asserting the `src/features/*/domain/**` threshold key exists in the coverage config with all four metrics at 100, so it cannot be deleted before phase 3. Its inertness today is proven by `test:coverage` passing. Vitest 4's behavior for a threshold glob matching zero files is confirmed empirically in M1 (it is configured from M1, not M3); if it errors rather than no-opping, the fallback is the post-coverage assertion script described in Risks.
  1064	- 111 - CI: `npm run build` runs `tsc -b` first.
  1065	- 112 - CI: `npm run size` is its own step and prints actual against limit for every entry of section 7.3 - 100 kB gzipped for the entry plus vendor pair, 15 kB for the stylesheet, 30 kB per route chunk, 5 kB per catalogue chunk. `build-output/size-limit-entries.test.ts` asserts `.size-limit.json` still carries those names and numbers, so a busted budget cannot be fixed by editing the budget without the edit showing up in the diff. It is a build-output test rather than a unit test - it runs under `verify:build`, not `npm test` - because it is meaningless before a `dist` exists, and an earlier draft called it a unit test while the layout placed it here. Which entries it expects is not a matter of judgement: `expected-build-output.json`'s `alwaysOn.sizeLimitEntries` holds the expected `{ name, limit }` array and the test compares `.size-limit.json` against it (section 7.1). The expectation lives in a different file from the thing it checks, which is what keeps the guard non-circular - comparing `.size-limit.json` against itself would pass any edit, defeating the whole point of the check. The array is the entry/vendor pair in M1, plus the stylesheet in M4, plus the routes and catalogues in M5, so there is exactly one correct content at each milestone. The earlier wording ("still carries those names and numbers", against a section listing seven entries) had two different correct answers at M1 and at M5, so an M1 implementer could not write it.
  1066	- 113 - CI: `npm run e2e` runs the flows listed, across the default and `development` projects.
  1067	- 114 - CI: `upload-artifact` with `if: always()`, asserted by the workflow-parse test. The one-off inspection of a deliberately failed run is a manual confirmation that the config does what it says, not a repeatable check - listed as review-dependent below rather than counted as a test.
  1068	- 115 - unit + e2e: injected clock and randomness throughout; the unit network stub; the Playwright global route handler. The discriminating part is mechanical: a lint rule bans `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `Date.now` and `new Date()` inside `src/**/*.test.*` and `e2e/**`, so a test reaching for a real timer fails lint rather than relying on nobody doing it. Injection seams alone never proved this, and the earlier entry implied they did.
  1069	- 116 - unit: the workflow-parse test asserts the `live-smoke` job's only trigger is `workflow_dispatch` and that it appears in no `needs` list.
  1070	- 116a, 116b - CI (manual): the dispatched run's log, captured to `evidence/live-smoke.txt`. The printed field names are read by a human, which is the point of the job; nothing asserts on them.
  1071	- 117 - CI: `setup-node` with `node-version-file: .nvmrc`; a unit test asserts `.nvmrc` and `package.json` `engines.node` agree.
  1072	- 118 - review: `VERIFICATION.md` and `README.md`'s command list. The workflow-parse test proves the commands exist; that they are documented where a contributor looks is a review judgement.
  1073	- 119 - review: the proof document cites runs, with evidence copied into `specs/phase-1-setup/evidence/`. Process, not a check.
  1074
  1075	### Deployment (120-126)
  1076
  1077	- 120, 121 - unit (the workflow-parse test asserts the `deploy` job's `if` condition, its `needs: verify`, and that its deploy step consumes the `site` artifact rather than running a build of its own) + CI (an actual pull-request run that does not deploy, and an actual `main` run that does). The artifact assertion is the one that discriminates: a deploy job that rebuilt would satisfy "deploys after the gates" while shipping bytes nothing verified.
  1078	- 122 - unit + e2e: a build-output test asserts every `src` and `href` in `dist/index.html` is root-relative (`/assets/...`), that no URL in `dist` carries a `/hierarchy-tree/` prefix left over from the previous hosting, and that `vite.config.ts` declares no `base` other than `/`. Static inspection cannot see a URL constructed at runtime, so the e2e half records every request the page issues (`page.on('request')`) across all routes and asserts each same-origin path resolves under `/` without a duplicated segment.
  1079	- 123 - deployed + CI: `deployed-smoke.spec.ts` against the live URL, after merge to `main`, with `DEPLOYED_BASE_URL` supplied to the `deployed` Playwright project. The CI half is the deploy job's assertion that `wrangler`'s reported `deployment-url` equals the `productionHostname` in `deployment.json` - the check that discriminates a production deployment from a preview when the Pages project's production branch was mis-set (invariant 126). A unit test additionally asserts that the hostname cited in `VERIFICATION.md` and `.env.example` matches `deployment.json`, so the documented value and the asserted value cannot diverge. Without it the smoke run tests a hostname the deploy never wrote to, and reports whatever was there before.
  1080	- 124 - deployed + script: the same spec loads `<base>/login` directly and reloads it, asserting the login placeholder both times AND that the response status is 200 - the rewrite rule serves `index.html` with a 200, so unlike the previous hosting's 404 fallback the status is part of the contract rather than something to look past. The build-output half asserts `dist/_redirects` exists and contains exactly the `/* /index.html 200` rule, so a missing or mistyped rule fails CI before any deploy.
  1081	- 125 - unit + review: the workflow-parse test asserts the deploy job's concurrency group and `cancel-in-progress: true`. That is configuration presence, not evidence that two concurrent pushes actually supersede rather than interleave - GitHub's scheduler owns the cancellation and Cloudflare owns deployment ordering, and neither is reproducible in this repository's test suite. The behavioral half is review-dependent and listed below.
  1082	- 126 - review + CI: manual, one-time setup outside the repository (the Cloudflare Pages project, its production branch set to `main`, and the two repository secrets). Named as a prerequisite in the milestone and in the pull-request description. Two of the three items diagnose themselves - a missing token or an unknown project fails the wrangler step with an explicit error - but the production-branch setting does NOT: it produces a successful upload to a preview URL. That is why invariant 123's deployment-URL assertion exists; it is the only mechanical check over any part of this invariant, and it converts the silent case into a failed job. The rest stays review-carried because it lives in a Cloudflare account no test can read.
  1083
  1084	- 126a - process: the post-merge obligation. `npm run e2e:deployed` runs against the recorded production hostname after the merge, its output is captured as `specs/phase-1-setup/evidence/deployed-smoke.txt`, and PROOF.md cites it for invariants 123 and 124. No milestone boundary and no pull-request run may mark those two as verified - M6's boundary explicitly excludes them. This is a process obligation rather than a check, and it is listed here so that "the phase is done" cannot be claimed from a green pull request alone.
  1085
  1086	### What must not be true (127-136)
  1087
  1088	- 127, 128, 129, 130 - script + lint, with the limits stated. The script matches at IDENTIFIER level, not by substring: it parses `src/**` and tests whole identifier segments against `make32`, `POISON_ARRAY`, `buildForest`, `flattenVisible`, plus string literals containing `/secrets` and the `role="tree"` attribute, with a stated allow-list for legitimate collisions (`encodeURIComponent`, `URLSearchParams`, `reportMissingKey`, `reportRootError`, `reportWebVitals`). A substring grep for `encode` and `report` - the earlier design - would have failed against the i18n and error-boundary modules this very spec requires, turning the first M3 commit red for the wrong reason. Storage access is additionally covered by the `no-restricted-globals` rule, which is the half that actually discriminates, because a grep can be defeated by renaming and the lint rule cannot be defeated by anything short of a disable comment (which `assert-no-secrets.mjs` greps for). Named honestly: these greps are a tripwire against accidental reintroduction, not a proof of absence, and they are listed below as partially review-dependent for that reason.
  1089	- 131 - unit: a test asserting `src/App.tsx`, `src/App.css`, `src/index.css`, `src/assets/` and `public/icons.svg` do not exist.
  1090	- 132 - review (see 96).
  1091	- 133 - script, in two halves that run at different times because they scan different things: `npm run lint` runs `assert-no-secrets.mjs --source-only` over `src`, and `npm run verify:build` runs `--bundle-only` over `dist` immediately after the build. The earlier single invocation inside `lint` claimed to scan `dist` while running three steps before `dist` existed, so the bundle was never scanned. `--bundle-only` FAILS on a missing `dist` rather than skipping. Both halves check: no `.env` file other than `.env.example` is tracked, no high-entropy hex or base64 literal above a length threshold, and none of `apiKey`, `authorization`, `bearer ` or a Firebase secret pattern. Entropy heuristics have false negatives by nature, which is why invariant 20's structural guarantee - nothing in configuration is secret, because the bundle is public - is the real protection and this script is the tripwire.
  1092	- 134 - unit: a test asserting `package.json`'s `dependencies` equals the expected allow-list exactly - `react`, `react-dom`, `react-router`, `zod`, `i18next`, `react-i18next`, `web-vitals`, and nothing else. A new runtime dependency fails the suite until the list is edited deliberately; `web-vitals` is on the list by the decision recorded at invariant 52, not by default.
  1093	- 135 - unit: the workflow-parse test asserts no `continue-on-error`, no `if: false`, and no skip flag on any verify step; a grep asserts no `.skip`, `.only` or `test.fixme` in `src` or `e2e`.
  1094	- 136 - review only. No mechanical check can distinguish an abstraction with no caller from a necessary seam. **Flagged as not mechanically checkable in this phase.**
  1095
  1096	### Invariants that are review-dependent
  1097
  1098	Both G1 reviewers found the earlier version of this section overstated - it listed ten invariants and then claimed "everything else has a check that fails", while several mapped checks would have passed against a broken implementation. Each of those was handled one of two ways: the check was strengthened so it discriminates (21, 32, 55, 56, 58, 59, 68, 76, 80, 86, 87, 91, 92, 99a, 100, 112, 115, 120, 122, 123, 128), or the invariant, or the specific half of it that no test reaches, was moved onto this list. The list below is the honest one. (This ledger previously cited 37 and 42, two of the retired caching invariants - a stale entry that left an auditor unable to tell whether the withdrawal had missed something. The numbers are retired, not reused, so they are simply gone from here.)
  1099
  1100	Fully review-dependent:
  1101
  1102	- 96, 96a, 132 - whether the placeholders promise nothing and carry no mockup chrome. A `lorem` grep is the only mechanical part.
  1103	- 118 - that the commands are documented where a contributor will look. The workflow-parse test proves they exist, not that they are findable.
  1104	- 119 - that the proof cites runs that happened. Process, not a check.
  1105	- 126 - the manual setup outside the repository: the Cloudflare Pages project and the two repository secrets.
  1106	- 136 - no abstraction built without a caller. No mechanical check distinguishes an unused abstraction from a necessary seam.
  1107
  1108	Partially review-dependent, with the covered half and the uncovered half named:
  1109
  1110	- 8 - the vocabulary grep covers exported names; "no domain type appears in a `shared` or `platform` signature" is review-carried in this phase, because no domain type exists yet for a check to find. It becomes mechanical in phase 3.
  1111	- 12 - the config-severity test pins the rules as errors; "argued in the decision log rather than made silently" is a review judgement about a diff.
  1112	- 102 - the workflow-parse test's command rule covers every GATING `run:` line, which is the `verify` job. The `deploy` job sits outside it by the invariant's own scoping, so its single permitted assertion (invariant 123's deployment-URL comparison) is bounded by review rather than by a test: a second `run:` line added to that job - the thing 102 says must not happen - fails nothing. Named here because this ledger claims to be the honest list, and this half of 102 became review-carried when the deploy job's assertion was admitted.
  1113	- 64 - the `no-restricted-syntax` rule bans the `toLocale*` methods; that `Intl` is used correctly is unobservable until phase 3 formats something.
  1114	- 72 - the contrast test walks `contrastPairs.ts` and fails on any listed pair below AA. That the list covers the pairs components actually use is review-carried; a component using an unlisted pair is caught by a reviewer, not by the test.
  1115	- 114 - the workflow-parse test asserts `if: always()`. The one-off inspection of a genuinely failed run is a manual confirmation, not a repeatable check.
  1116	- 125 - the workflow-parse test asserts the concurrency group and `cancel-in-progress`. That two concurrent pushes actually supersede is GitHub scheduler behavior, not reproducible here.
  1117	- 127, 128, 129, 130 - the identifier-level script plus the storage lint rules are a tripwire against accidental reintroduction. A determined rename or a constructed string defeats the script; the lint rules and the absence of any repository module are the load-bearing parts. For 128 specifically, the identifier-and-member ban plus the e2e storage-emptiness assertion (section 2.4) covers the static and the observable-effect case; a write performed through a computed member access on a storage global is caught only if it actually writes, which the e2e assertion sees and lint cannot.
  1118
  1119	- File and module naming conventions (section 1) - review only, and declared non-binding there. No lint rule, script or structural test checks filenames, barrels, named exports or `memo` usage, so a kebab-case module or an unmemoized component passes the whole pipeline. The one case where a name is load-bearing rather than stylistic - the emitted route chunk names the `size-limit` globs and invariant 89's assertions are written against - is covered mechanically by those globs failing on no match, which does not depend on the convention being honoured.
  1120	- 133 - entropy and pattern heuristics have false negatives by nature. Invariant 20's structural guarantee is the real protection.
  1121
  1122	For everything not named in this section, the mapping above names a check intended to fail against a broken implementation. That is a design intent stated per invariant, not a blanket guarantee: the previous two versions of this sentence claimed more than the map delivered, and a reviewer should treat any individual entry as a claim to be checked rather than as a certification. Where an entry's check turns out not to discriminate once the code exists, the honest response is to strengthen it or move the invariant onto this list, not to leave the sentence standing.
  1123

    13	// The testable startup path: main.tsx is the one file whose name is not
    14	// ours to choose (fixed by index.html's <script src>), so the actual
    15	// startup logic - including the configuration-failure branch (invariants
    16	// 15, 16) - lives here where a test can call it directly.
    17	export async function bootstrap(
    18	  container: Element,
    19	  configurationResult: ConfigurationResult,
    20	): Promise<void> {
    21	  if (!configurationResult.ok) {
    22	    // A minimal, safe-defaults observability instance (console sink,
    23	    // error level): the real one createRuntime.ts builds needs validated
    24	    // configuration, which is unavailable here by definition. No router,
    25	    // no feature code and no partially configured UI is mounted either way.
    26	    const { facade } = createObservability({
    27	      configuration: { observabilitySink: 'console', logLevel: 'error' },
    28	      randomness: createSystemRandomness(),
    29	    });
    30	    facade.logger.error('app.configuration_invalid', {
    31	      invalidKeys: configurationResult.invalidKeys,
    32	    });
    33	    createRoot(container).render(
    34	      createElement(
    35	        StrictMode,
    36	        null,
    37	        createElement(ConfigurationErrorScreen, {
    38	          invalidKeys: configurationResult.invalidKeys,
    39	        }),
    40	      ),
    41	    );
    42	    return;
    43	  }
    44
    45	  const runtime = await createRuntime(configurationResult.configuration);
    46	  const router = createApplicationRouter(runtime);
    47	  runtime.interactionTracker.attach(router);
    48
    49	  function handleBoundaryError(error: unknown): void {
    50	    // React 19 logs every boundary-caught error via console.error by
    51	    // default; routing it to reportRootError instead is what keeps the
    52	    // console clean for invariant 100's e2e assertion, with the error
    53	    // recorded in the buffer where that assertion actually looks.
    54	    reportRootError(error, {
    55	      observability: runtime.observability,
    56	      interactionTracker: runtime.interactionTracker,
    57	    });
    58	  }
    59
    60	  createRoot(container, {
    61	    onCaughtError: handleBoundaryError,
    62	    onUncaughtError: handleBoundaryError,
    63	  }).render(
    64	    createElement(
    65	      StrictMode,
    66	      null,
    67	      createElement(ApplicationRoot, {
    68	        runtime,
    69	        children: createElement(RouterProvider, { router }),
    70	      }),
    71	    ),
    72	  );
    73	}

    28	export async function createRuntime(
    29	  configuration: Configuration,
    30	): Promise<Runtime> {
    31	  const randomness = createSystemRandomness();
    32	  const clock = createSystemClock();
    33
    34	  const { facade: observability, bufferHandle } = createObservability({
    35	    configuration,
    36	    randomness,
    37	  });
    38
    39	  if (configuration.telemetryBufferHandle && bufferHandle !== null) {
    40	    globalThis.__hierarchyTreeTelemetry = bufferHandle;
    41	  }
    42
    43	  const interactionTracker = createInteractionTracker(observability);
    44
    45	  const http = createHttpClient({
    46	    transport: createFetchTransport(),
    47	    clock,
    48	    randomness,
    49	    observability,
    50	    configuration,
    51	    correlationId: () =>
    52	      interactionTracker.currentCorrelationId() ??
    53	      createCorrelationId(randomness),
    54	  });
    55
    56	  const i18n = await createInternationalization({
    57	    resources: { common: commonCatalogue },
    58	    language: RUNTIME_LANGUAGE,
    59	    observability,
    60	  });
    61
    62	  return Object.freeze({
    63	    configuration,
    64	    observability,
    65	    http,
    66	    i18n,
    67	    interactionTracker,

     8	// resolving, so a route never renders before its namespace is registered
     9	// (invariant 62). No loader, no guard, no redirect - this phase's routes
    10	// resolve to a component and nothing else (invariant 97).
    11	export function routeDefinitions(
    12	  instance: i18n,
    13	  developmentRoutes: boolean,
    14	): RouteObject[] {
    15	  const children: RouteObject[] = [
    16	    {
    17	      index: true,
    18	      lazy: async () => {
    19	        const { HomeRoute, loadTranslations } =
    20	          await import('./routes/HomeRoute');
    21	        await loadTranslations(instance);
    22	        return { Component: HomeRoute };
    23	      },
    24	    },
    25	    {
    26	      path: 'login',
    27	      lazy: async () => {
    28	        const { LoginRoute, loadTranslations } =
    29	          await import('./routes/LoginRoute');
    30	        await loadTranslations(instance);
    31	        return { Component: LoginRoute };
    32	      },
    33	    },
    34	  ];
    35
    36	  // Gated on both the Vite build-time DEV flag, read directly here rather
    37	  // than through environment.ts's re-exported isDevelopmentBuild (that
    38	  // re-export does not fold across the module boundary, so the bundler
    39	  // could not drop the module or its chunk from the production bundle -
    40	  // invariant 86b; see the eslint.config.js override on this file), and
    41	  // the runtime flag (what the configuration schema and e2e suite
    42	  // express). Registered before the wildcard, which would otherwise match
    43	  // `/__kit` first and render not-found instead.
    44	  if (import.meta.env.DEV && developmentRoutes) {
    45	    children.push({
    46	      path: '__kit',
    47	      lazy: async () => {
    48	        const { KitRoute } = await import('../kit-route/KitRoute');
    49	        return { Component: KitRoute };
    50	      },
    51	    });
    52	  }
    53
    54	  children.push({
    55	    path: '*',
    56	    lazy: async () => {
    57	      const { NotFoundRoute } = await import('./routes/NotFoundRoute');
    58	      return { Component: NotFoundRoute };
    59	    },
    60	  });
    61
    62	  return [
    63	    {
    64	      path: '/',
    65	      element: createElement(ApplicationLayout),
    66	      ErrorBoundary: RouteErrorBoundary,
    67	      // Every child route is lazy(), so the router needs SOMETHING to
    68	      // paint during the first chunk fetch; without it react-router warns
    69	      // "No `HydrateFallback` element provided" on every initial load,
    70	      // which invariant 100's empty console allow-list does not tolerate.
    71	      // Nothing routes to the fallback in a way a user perceives - the
    72	      // chunks are sub-kilobyte - so it renders nothing rather than
    73	      // introducing a designed loading state this phase has no other use
    74	      // for.
    75	      HydrateFallback: () => null,
    76	      children,
    77	    },
    78	  ];
    79	}

    15	export type InteractionTracker = {
    16	  attach: (router: Router) => () => void;
    17	  currentCorrelationId: () => string | null;
    18	  // Primitive-throw dedup for reportRootError.ts (invariant 92): a WeakSet
    19	  // covers object errors, but WeakSet.add rejects primitives outright, so
    20	  // they need this string-keyed sibling instead. Scoped to the current
    21	  // interaction rather than the tracker's whole lifetime, so a genuinely
    22	  // repeated primitive throw in a LATER interaction is reported again.
    23	  shouldReportPrimitive: (key: string) => boolean;
    24	};
    25
    26	export function createInteractionTracker(
    27	  observability: Pick<ObservabilityFacade, 'tracer' | 'analytics'>,
    28	): InteractionTracker {
    29	  let correlationId: string | null = null;
    30	  let tracking = false;
    31	  let reportedPrimitives = new Set<string>();
    32
    33	  function startInteraction(): void {
    34	    tracking = true;
    35	    correlationId = observability.tracer.startInteraction();
    36	    reportedPrimitives = new Set();
    37	  }
    38
    39	  function settle(state: RouterState): void {
    40	    tracking = false;
    41	    if (state.errors && Object.keys(state.errors).length > 0) {
    42	      return;
    43	    }
    44	    const routeId = state.matches[state.matches.length - 1]?.route.id;
    45	    if (routeId === undefined) return;
    46	    observability.analytics.track('app.route_viewed', { routeId });
    47	  }
    48
    49	  function attach(router: Router): () => void {
    50	    startInteraction();
    51	    return router.subscribe((state) => {
    52	      const isNavigating = state.navigation.state !== 'idle';
    53	      if (isNavigating && !tracking) {
    54	        startInteraction();
    55	        return;
    56	      }
    57	      if (!isNavigating && tracking) {
    58	        settle(state);
    59	      }
    60	    });
    61	  }
    62
    63	  function shouldReportPrimitive(key: string): boolean {
    64	    if (reportedPrimitives.has(key)) return false;
    65	    reportedPrimitives.add(key);
    66	    return true;
    67	  }
    68
    69	  return {
    70	    attach,
    71	    currentCorrelationId: () => correlationId,
    72	    shouldReportPrimitive,
    73	  };
    74	}
     1	import type { ObservabilityFacade } from '@platform/observability';
     2	import type { InteractionTracker } from '../routing';
     3
     4	// Object identity is tracked globally rather than per instance - identity
     5	// is global, and a WeakSet self-empties, so no explicit lifecycle owns it.
     6	// This is what survives StrictMode's double-invoked effects: a useRef
     7	// guard does not, because the component mounts twice.
     8	const reportedObjects = new WeakSet<object>();
     9
    10	export type ReportRootErrorDependencies = {
    11	  observability: Pick<ObservabilityFacade, 'logger' | 'tracer' | 'analytics'>;
    12	  interactionTracker: InteractionTracker;
    13	};
    14
    15	export function reportRootError(
    16	  error: unknown,
    17	  { observability, interactionTracker }: ReportRootErrorDependencies,
    18	): string {
    19	  const correlationId =
    20	    interactionTracker.currentCorrelationId() ??
    21	    observability.tracer.startInteraction();
    22
    23	  if (!shouldReport(error, interactionTracker)) {
    24	    return correlationId;
    25	  }
    26
    27	  observability.logger.error('app.error_boundary_shown', {
    28	    correlationId,
    29	    message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
    30	  });
    31	  observability.analytics.track('app.error_boundary_shown', {
    32	    correlationId,
    33	  });
    34
    35	  return correlationId;
    36	}
    37
    38	// WeakSet.add throws TypeError on a primitive, which is reachable here:
    39	// `throw 'boom'`, `throw null` and a promise rejected with a primitive
    40	// all occur, from third-party code and from React Router's own thrown
    41	// responses.
    42	function shouldReport(
    43	  error: unknown,
    44	  interactionTracker: InteractionTracker,
    45	): boolean {
    46	  if (typeof error === 'object' && error !== null) {
    47	    if (reportedObjects.has(error)) return false;
    48	    reportedObjects.add(error);
    49	    return true;
    50	  }
    51	  return interactionTracker.shouldReportPrimitive(
    52	    `${typeof error}:${String(error)}`,
    53	  );
    54	}

    16	// Catches everything RouteErrorBoundary can't - it renders above
    17	// RouterProvider, so useNavigate() is unavailable here; recovery is a
    18	// full document load back to the app root instead.
    19	export class RootErrorBoundary extends Component<
    20	  RootErrorBoundaryProps,
    21	  RootErrorBoundaryState
    22	> {
    23	  override state: RootErrorBoundaryState = {
    24	    hasError: false,
    25	    correlationId: null,
    26	  };
    27
    28	  static getDerivedStateFromError(): Partial<RootErrorBoundaryState> {
    29	    return { hasError: true };
    30	  }
    31
    32	  override componentDidCatch(error: unknown): void {
    33	    const correlationId = reportRootError(error, {
    34	      observability: this.props.runtime.observability,
    35	      interactionTracker: this.props.runtime.interactionTracker,
    36	    });
    37	    this.setState({ correlationId });
    38	  }
    39
    40	  private handleRecover = (): void => {
    41	    window.location.assign(this.props.runtime.configuration.basePath);
    42	  };
    43
    44	  override render(): ReactNode {
    45	    if (this.state.hasError) {
    46	      return (
    47	        <ErrorSurface
    48	          correlationId={this.state.correlationId ?? ''}
    49	          onRecover={this.handleRecover}
    50	        />
    51	      );
    52	    }
    53	    return this.props.children;
    54	  }
    55	}

     5	export type ConfigurationResult =
     6	  | { ok: true; configuration: Configuration }
     7	  | { ok: false; invalidKeys: readonly string[] };
     8
     9	// VITE_LOG_LEVEL and VITE_OBSERVABILITY_SINK default differently per mode
    10	// (development/production/test) - resolved here, before the schema's own
    11	// static .default() acts as the fallback for an unrecognized MODE.
    12	function withModeAppropriateDefaults(raw: RawEnvironment): RawEnvironment {
    13	  const isDevelopment = raw.MODE === 'development';
    14	  const isTest = raw.MODE === 'test';
    15
    16	  return {
    17	    ...raw,
    18	    VITE_LOG_LEVEL: raw.VITE_LOG_LEVEL ?? (isDevelopment ? 'debug' : 'warn'),
    19	    VITE_OBSERVABILITY_SINK:
    20	      raw.VITE_OBSERVABILITY_SINK ??
    21	      (isTest ? 'none' : isDevelopment ? 'console' : 'buffer'),
    22	    VITE_DEVELOPMENT_ROUTES:
    23	      raw.VITE_DEVELOPMENT_ROUTES ?? String(isDevelopment),
    24	  };
    25	}
    26
    27	export function createConfiguration(raw: RawEnvironment): ConfigurationResult {
    28	  const result = configurationSchema.safeParse(
    29	    withModeAppropriateDefaults(raw),
    30	  );
    31
    32	  if (!result.success) {
    33	    // Only the offending key names, never their values (invariant 17).
    34	    const invalidKeys = [
    35	      ...new Set(result.error.issues.map((issue) => String(issue.path[0]))),
    36	    ];
    37	    return { ok: false, invalidKeys };
    38	  }
    39
    40	  const configuration: Configuration = Object.freeze({
    41	    apiBaseUrl: result.data.VITE_API_BASE_URL,
    42	    logLevel: result.data.VITE_LOG_LEVEL,
    43	    observabilitySink: result.data.VITE_OBSERVABILITY_SINK,
    44	    requestTimeoutMilliseconds: result.data.VITE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MILLISECONDS,
    45	    telemetryBufferHandle: result.data.VITE_FEATURE_TELEMETRY_BUFFER_HANDLE,
    46	    developmentRoutes: result.data.VITE_DEVELOPMENT_ROUTES,
    47	    basePath: result.data.BASE_URL,
    48	  });
    49
    50	  return { ok: true, configuration };
    51	}

    13	export async function createInternationalization(

    12	  small: 'h-6 w-6 text-xs',
    13	  medium: 'h-[34px] w-[34px] text-sm',
    14	};

    19	};

    21	export const Avatar = memo(function Avatar({
    22	  imageSource,
    23	  displayName,
    24	  size,
    25	  decorative,
    26	}: AvatarProps) {
    27	  const [imageFailed, setImageFailed] = useState(false);
    28	  const showImage = imageSource !== undefined && !imageFailed;
    29
    30	  if (showImage) {
    31	    return (
    32	      <img
    33	        src={imageSource}
    34	        width={SIZE_PIXELS[size]}
    35	        height={SIZE_PIXELS[size]}
    36	        loading="lazy"
    37	        referrerPolicy="no-referrer"
    38	        alt={decorative ? '' : displayName}
    39	        onError={() => setImageFailed(true)}
    40	        className={`${SIZE_CLASS[size]} rounded-full object-cover`}
    41	      />
    42	    );
    43	  }
    44
    45	  return (
    46	    <span
    47	      aria-hidden={decorative || undefined}
    48	      aria-label={decorative ? undefined : displayName}
    49	      className={`${SIZE_CLASS[size]} flex items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-primary-tint font-medium text-ink`}

    20	  variant,
    21	  type = 'button',
    22	  disabled,
    23	  busy,
    24	  onClick,
    25	  children,
    26	}: ButtonProps) {
    27	  const handleClick = useCallback(

    29	      if (busy) {
    30	        // Blocking means both halves: skip the caller's onClick AND stop

    37	    },

    39	  );

    44	      disabled={disabled}
    45	      aria-busy={busy ? 'true' : undefined}
    46	      aria-disabled={busy ? 'true' : undefined}
    47	      onClick={handleClick}
    48	      className={`duration-fast rounded-control px-4 py-2 font-medium transition-colors ease-standard disabled:opacity-50 ${VARIANT_CLASS[variant]}`}

    52	  );

    14	export const Field = memo(function Field({
    15	  id,
    16	  label,
    17	  hint,
    18	  error,
    19	  required,
    20	  children,
    21	}: FieldProps) {
    22	  const hintId = hint !== undefined ? `${id}-hint` : undefined;
    23	  const errorId = error !== undefined ? `${id}-error` : undefined;
    24	  const describedBy = [hintId, errorId].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || undefined;
    25
    26	  const contextValue = useMemo(
    27	    () => ({
    28	      invalid: error !== undefined,
    29	      required: Boolean(required),
    30	      ...(describedBy !== undefined ? { describedBy } : {}),
    31	    }),
    32	    [describedBy, error, required],
    33	  );
    34
    35	  return (
    36	    <div>
    37	      <label htmlFor={id}>{label}</label>
    38	      <FieldContext.Provider value={contextValue}>
    39	        {children}
    40	      </FieldContext.Provider>
    41	      {hint !== undefined && <p id={hintId}>{hint}</p>}
    42	      {error !== undefined && (
    43	        <p id={errorId} role="alert">
    44	          {error}
    45	        </p>
    46	      )}
    47	    </div>
    48	  );
    49	});

473:- Timeout (invariant 23): ONE deadline per logical request, not one per attempt. `createHttpClient.ts` arms a single `AbortController` and a single `clock.setTimer(timeoutMilliseconds)` when the call begins, and that one signal is composed into every attempt and into the backoff wait. A caller passing 8000 ms therefore waits at most 8000 ms in total, covering the first attempt, the backoff and the retry - which is what invariant 23 now requires and what the per-attempt design contradicted. The deadline timer is cleared through its cancel handle when the call settles, so a completed request leaves no pending timer. The abort reason distinguishes a deadline abort from a caller abort, which is how the client returns `{ kind: 'timeout' }` rather than a `cancelled` outcome.
474:- Signal composition (invariant 24): `AbortSignal.any([callerSignal, deadlineController.signal])` when the caller supplies one. `AbortSignal.any` is Baseline in all target browsers and in Node 24, so no polyfill is added (invariant 134).
475:- Caller abort (invariant 25): if `callerSignal.aborted` after a failure, the client returns without retrying and emits no error-level record - one debug-level record noting the cancellation.

523:- Missing keys (invariant 63): two DIFFERENT i18next hooks do the two halves of this, and conflating them was a validation finding. `missingKeyHandler` is a void notification callback - i18next ignores whatever it returns - so it does the reporting: `observability.logger.error('i18n.missing_key', { namespace, key })`, plus, under test, a push to a module-level array that `vitest.setup.ts` clears in `beforeEach` and asserts empty in `afterEach`, so any rendered surface requesting a nonexistent key fails the suite. `parseMissingKeyHandler` is the hook whose RETURN VALUE is rendered, so it produces the visibly wrong marker. 765:`createFakeClock` is a manually-advanced timer queue, not an instantly-resolving `sleep`. It implements the production `Clock` interface exactly - `now()`, `setTimer(delay, callback)` returning a cancel handle, and `wait(delay, signal?)` - and adds one test-only method, `advance(milliseconds)`. Matching the injected interface including `wait`'s optional `AbortSignal` is what makes it a substitute rather than an approximation; a fake declaring `sleep(delay)` would not satisfy the type the client is written against, and an abort arriving during the backoff wait is a real path the deadline exercises, where `advance` moves `now` forward and fires every timer whose deadline has passed, in deadline order, awaiting the microtask queue between each. Nothing fires until a test says so. The earlier design - an instantly-resolving `sleep` - could not serve both jobs the http client needs from a clock: the deadline is armed through the same clock as the backoff, so a `sleep(timeout).then(abort)` would resolve on the next microtask and abort every request before its fake transport could respond. Which of the two won would depend on microtask ordering inside the fake, making the entire `src/platform/http` suite non-deterministic while appearing to pass. `setTimer` returning a cancel handle is also what lets the client clear the deadline on a successful response instead of leaking a pending timer per request.
773:- `webServer: { command: 'npm run preview -- --port 4173', url: 'http://127.0.0.1:4173/', reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI }` - the suite runs against the production build (invariant 113), not the dev server. It **serves the existing `dist` and does not rebuild it**. An earlier draft ran `npm run build && npm run preview`, which in CI (where `reuseExistingServer` is false) rebuilt `dist` during the e2e step - after `verify:build` and `size` had inspected the previous one and before the `site` artifact was uploaded from it. The bytes that shipped would then be bytes no gate had ever inspected, contradicting invariant 120's central claim, and the workflow-parse check named to discriminate ("the deploy step consumes the artifact rather than building its own") passes against that arrangement, so nothing would have caught it. Locally the build is the developer's own `npm run build`; in CI it is the workflow's build step, three steps earlier. `vite preview` fails loudly on a missing `dist`, so the ordering error surfaces as an error rather than as a stale pass.
